#2221. EFL expert drops ‘exciting’ West Brom promotion prediction

West Brom are positioned in 5th place in the Championship table after 15 fixtures and are in the play-offs along with Stoke City, Wolves, Swansea City, Southampton and QPR. WBA are only a point behind joint-top Birmingham City and Middlesbrough.

The Baggies beat Millwall 3-0 at The Hawthorns last time out before the international break. Isaac Price, Jayson Molumby and Felix Horn Myhre got their goals against the Lions as they secured another eye-catching win.

Elek has been impressed with the Midlands outfit and has delivered his verdict on the latest episode of the Not The 20 Podcast on YouTube: “They have been absolutely phenomenal in the past couple of games. They’ve gone from a team I thought are going to start well and then drop off to a relegation scrap. They’ve proven me completely wrong. In 5th place, a point off top spot. Talking about can Birmingham maintain this, can West Brom? The answer is yes. The numbers are good, the performances are good. The results are good. The players are good. It’s all looking quite exciting.”

West Brom endured a tough past campaign and churned through both Ryan Mason and Eric Ramsay before they settled on James Morrison. WBA were in a relegation battle before Morrison managed to keep them up in the end.

Morrison has managed to steady the ship with the Baggies and has done a solid job. His side are now in the top eight and are eyeing the Premier League.

It was a busy summer for them and they ended up bringing in the likes of Jimmy-Jay Morgan, Barney Stewart and Rabby Nzingoula, among others, to bolster their ranks. They also cut ties with players including Alex Mowatt, Jed Wallace and Karlan Grant to help free up space and funds to pave the way for reinforcements.

West Brom opted to go for young and hungry players in the last transfer window and they now have a nice blend of youth and experience at their diposal. Morrison will get the opportunity to sign some more new faces in January if needed ahead of the second-half of this term.

As Elek has alluded to, West Brom should be considered genuine promotion contenders. WBA are solid at the back and have threats at the top end of the pitch.

In goalkeeper Max O’Leary, they have an experienced stopper who knows the league well and is a safe pair of hands. Defender George Campbell has become one of their most prized assets in defence alongside the know-how of Nat Phillips and/or Chris Mepham.

Nzingoula, Molumby and Ousmane Diakite have bags of energy in the middle of the park, whilst Horn Myhre and Price have quality to hurt opposition defenders. Up top, Morgan has a very bright future ahead of him in the game and the Baggies’ decision to sign him earlier this year was a masterstroke.

West Brom are back in action on Saturday 21st October with an away trip to Swansea City. They should be in confident mood ahead of their trek down to South Wales.

#2220. Liam Scales' honest Celtic form verdict after avoiding 'nightmare' vs Kilmarnock

It wasn't pretty and it wasn't memorable, but as is usually the case under Martin O'Neill, Celtic got the job done.

The manager couldn't have picked a kinder fixture – at home against the side bottom of the table – for his team to return to winning ways in the Premiership. Yet Celtic made hard work of beating Kilmarnock.

Sam Johnstone produced a crucial double save inside the opening minute to deny Tom Lowery and if Ieuan Owen had connected cleanly with Erik Ring's cross in stoppage time, Celtic would be back in crisis mode. Alas, the hosts held on.

Liam Scales' first-half finish proved decisive on an afternoon permeated with missed chances for both sides.

The slender victory restored Celtic's four-point lead at the Premiership summit going into the international break, although Rangers have a game in hand.

They took care of Besiktas midweek, but O'Neill's reigning champions hadn't won in the league in a fortnight, losing to Falkirk and drawing with Dundee United, underlining the significance of Sunday's win.

"It was definitely important," Scales said. "Two games [in the league] without a win is bad enough, but three would have been a nightmare.

"We knew we needed that win and can go into the break and refresh. Some of the lads can rest and recover and hopefully we’ll come back in this form.

"I do think confidence is a massive part of our group and it was probably hit a little bit. The win against a top side like Besiktas has boosted us a little bit. There’s kind of a better mood around. We just want to keep adding good results."

Celtic's Liam Scales celebrates with his team-mates. (Image: Steve Welsh/PA)

Celtic entered the last international break following three consecutive losses to Rangers, Ferencvaros and Rangers again.

Things felt ominous, with O'Neill publicly considering his future after the second of those derby defeats.

But Celtic rallied and defeated Motherwell in their first game back. Things weren't smooth over the following eight matches, but as players return from injury, Scales feels positive about the future.

"We had Yang back on Sunday, Jota is obviously starting. These guys are getting back to full sharpness and getting minutes," he said. "Hopefully this will help and we can build on it.

"We know we haven’t been good enough between the last international window and this one. We’ve let a few results go and we’re not exactly where we want to be.

"It was just really important to win these last two games before the break and be in a good place for coming back."

Celtic leading the league was rare last season. Only in the dying minutes of the campaign did they return to the Premiership summit after Hearts knocked them off their perch back in September 2025.

"We always want to be on top of the table. We don’t want to be chasing," Scales stated. "We want to be a good arm’s length from the challengers.

"That is the goal all season – to stay top. It’s important to us but obviously there are so many games to play. You go through really busy spells and both teams will be challenged. But we are just happy where we are now.

"It hasn’t been spoken about – but it doesn’t need to be spoken about. We all know the standards at this club that have been set over a number of years.

"It doesn’t need to be discussed where we want to be – because it’s top of the table. Last season wasn’t what we wanted at all and we don’t want a repeat of that."

Scales scored his second goal in four games against Kilmarnock, connecting sweetly with Camilo Duran's looped cross.

The Irishman's effort sailed over opposition goalkeeper Nico Mantl and into the back of the net to break the deadlock in the 26th minute.

"It took an age to come down," Scales reflected. "I wasn’t sure if it was going to land on the roof of the net. I was just trying to guide it on target and luckily enough it went in.

"I don’t really have a target for goals – it’s more about clean sheets for me. But it’s nice. We’ve done a lot of work on set pieces, we’re getting the ball into the box more rather than going short and I suppose you always get a bit excited as a centre half when you go forward for a corner.

"It is nice to score and hopefully I can get a few more between now and the end of the season. I felt we should have killed the game in the second half. We were unlucky not to score.

"When you are only a goal up the atmosphere can get a bit nervy and that can translate onto the pitch. But I don’t think we were troubled too much. It was comfortable but it would have looked better if we’d scored some more."

For goals this season, Scales is now level with Kasper Hogh. The striker thought he'd ended his 16-game scoring drought on Sunday, only for VAR to intervene and disallow the strike for a foul in the build-up by Mika Baur.

Hogh didn't let his frustrations boil over, instead working even harder and offering a useful focal point in attack.

He earned the in-stadium man of the match award and was deservedly applauded off the field in the 71st minute. Scales is certain the goals will come, even if he snatched one from Hogh against Kilmarnock.

"He’s been brilliant. He keeps doing the right things and eventually it will fall for him," the defender added. "He was so unlucky with his goal being ruled out.

"And he told me he was right behind me with the goal I scored! If I’d known that I might have left it!

"It will fall for him. He’s a goal scorer and a good player. His all-round game was brilliant, he held the ball up really well. He’s just been unlucky. But his attitude has been brilliant.

"If he keeps doing the right things it will work out for him. He has an amazing attitude and that’s why I really believe he will be successful."

#2219. FIGC, Galliani e Malagò davanti al TFN: voto del 14 dicembre a rischio

La Federazione si costituisce nel procedimento sulla commissione incaricata di controllare le candidature.

La FIGC ha deciso di costituirsi davanti al Tribunale Federale Nazionale nel procedimento avviato dal ricorso di Adriano Galliani contro la commissione nominata da Giovanni Malagò per verificare le candidature alla presidenza federale. Secondo quanto riportato da Onefootball, Il TFN ascolterà le parti prima di pronunciarsi collegialmente. La controversia potrebbe far slittare le elezioni, per ora fissate al 14 dicembre.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Secondo Onefootball, il calendario della procedura è già stretto: l’elenco dei candidati ammessi dovrebbe essere pubblicato entro il 14 novembre. Il limite stabilito dal CONI per celebrare l’assemblea elettiva resta il 31 gennaio 2027.

Galliani ha presentato il ricorso lunedì 9 novembre tramite il proprio legale, l’avvocato Filippo Lattanzi. L’atto riguarda la commissione istituita il 2 novembre da Malagò, commissario straordinario della FIGC e a sua volta candidato alla presidenza. All’organismo è stato affidato il controllo della regolarità delle candidature.

Per Galliani, la commissione non sarebbe prevista dalle norme statutarie e regolamentari della Federazione e non avrebbe quindi titolo per effettuare quelle verifiche. Il ricorso contesta anche la scelta di istituirla da parte di Malagò, direttamente coinvolto nella competizione elettorale.

La richiesta al TFN è di sospendere in via cautelare l’efficacia del provvedimento e poi annullarlo. Secondo la posizione sostenuta da Galliani, il controllo delle candidature dovrebbe essere svolto dagli organi già individuati dalle norme federali, in particolare dalla Segreteria generale e dal segretario Marco Brunelli. Galliani è sostenuto da Assocalciatori e Assoallenatori.

Nel confronto sulle candidature ha un peso anche la posizione del Genoa. In un primo momento l’amministratore delegato rossoblù Andres Blazquez aveva sottoscritto l’accredito a favore di Galliani. Successivamente il presidente Dan Sucu ha espresso il sostegno del club a Malagò, accompagnandolo con una comunicazione formale di revoca e diffida relativa alla precedente adesione.

Malagò ha presentato undici accrediti di club di Serie A, esattamente il minimo richiesto. Se quello del Genoa non fosse considerato valido, uno degli undici sostegni necessari verrebbe meno e la candidatura potrebbe non soddisfare il requisito previsto.

Il ricorso di Galliani, però, non chiede direttamente l’esclusione di Malagò. Il suo oggetto principale è la legittimità della commissione incaricata dei controlli. La posizione del Genoa resta un elemento del contenzioso e potrebbe assumere rilievo nella successiva valutazione dei requisiti.

#2218. Lo Monaco: "Napoli, a gennaio devi farti due domande. Mi mangio le mani per 3 giocatori"

"I mercati non sono quelli che cominciano e finiscono nei tempi canonici". A Radio Napoli Centrale parla così Pietro Lo Monaco, commentando presente e futuro della squadra partenopea: "A gennaio, la domanda che si deve porre il Napoli è sulla situazione generale: la rifondazione che doveva cominciare in estate, la vogliamo far partire a gennaio? La si vuole dividere in due tranche e completarla in estate? Sono domande alle quali vanno date risposte".

"Il Napoli ha bisogno di rivitalizzare la rosa. A centrocampo hai Anguissa, ma andrà via perché in scadenza e a questo punto ci vuole anche un atto di coraggio, magari una risoluzione. Mi mangio le mani per Cisse, Liberali, Doumbia. Tanti giocatori potevano essere presi a prezzi accessibili. Non per forza devi sempre vincere, certe volte ci sta che certi giocatori hanno chiuso e fatto il loro tempo. E se non ci sono richieste, vanno comunque mandati da qualche parte. Lucca per esempio se la fa addosso, è un ectoplasma. Ogni volta che va in possesso palla, tende ad andare sempre a terra. Ha paura. La maglia del Napoli pesa per lui, sarebbe disumano.

"Lang è un altro giocatore che difficilmente darà più di questo. Rafa Marin è un ripescato, era stato già bocciato. Se si considerano i soldi spesi per Lucca, Beukema, Lang, sono cento milioni: ma quanti se ne recuperano? Lang ad esempio in ammortamento può essere venduto a 15 milioni di euro. Le domande te le devi porre, ma devi anche darti risposte. E devi prendere decisioni"

#2216. The 3 summer targets Blackburn Rovers should pursue again in January, including Balazs Toth replacement

Blackburn Rovers have exceeded the expectations of many in the early stages of the 2026/27 campaign. Tony Mowbray‘s side sit 13th in the Championship after 15 games, when many expected them to be in the thick of a relegation battle.

That fate could yet await with a lot of the season left to play, but spirits are fairly high at Ewood Park. There is no hiding that the Rovers squad needs work though, with only three new summer signings failing to suitably reinforce the ranks.

New targets will be on the radar, but Blackburn Rovers identified some smart options in the summer who could be available this winter. Here, we put forward three summer targets who should be back on the radar ahead of January…

Balazs Toth has continued to resist Blackburn Rovers’ new contract efforts. It remains to be seen exactly when he leaves, but a departure seemingly awaits at some point in 2027, and the club could do with sourcing a replacement sooner rather than later.

Alex Palmer was linked with a move to Ewood Park in the last transfer window, and he could be a fine option to consider to replace Toth. The 30-year-old is out of favour at Ipswich Town under Gary O’Neil, but he is a proven Championship goalkeeper who could quickly become a dependable No. 1 for Mowbray.

Palmer is under contract until 2028 at Portman Road but given that he has not made a Premier League matchday squad this season, the Tractor Boys should not have an issue letting him go for a fairly cheap fee.

Blackburn Rovers have one of Europe’s most clinical strikers in Andri Gudjohnsen at the moment, but competition beyond him is limited. Yuki Ohashi is the only other out-and-out centre-forward, so more depth would not go amiss.

Daniel Jebbison was targeted by Rovers in the summer and a loan-to-buy deal was even agreed, but he ended up staying at Bournemouth. Given the fact that he has played only four times so far this season, the 23-year-old would benefit from a winter move elsewhere to find more game time.

The Canadian striker has Championship experience and has strong physical traits like Gudjohnsen. Jebbison is a strong finisher on both feet and Mowbray’s style of play and ability to develop players could help him hit prolific form.

Last but not least is a much-needed midfield reinforcement. Mowbray has expressed a desire to sign a new central midfielder in the winter, and someone who offers experience but has more years ahead of Sam Morsy and Adam Forshaw would be ideal.

Alan Browne fits this profile perfectly. The 31-year-old has played over 400 Championship games but showed on loan at Middlesbrough last season that he still has plenty in the tank, offering a well-rounded skillset, versatility and energy in the middle of the park.

Browne is way down the pecking order at Sunderland and out of contract next summer. It should be an easy deal for Blackburn Rovers to strike and he would instantly improve their options in midfield.

#2214. Sassuolo, c’è l’ufficialità: Roberto D'Aversa è il nuovo allenatore

L’ex tecnico granata è il nuovo allenatore del Sassuolo fino al 2027

Il Sassuolo ha ufficializzato il nome del successore dell'esonerato Alberto Aquilani, affidando la panchina a Roberto D'Aversa. Il tecnico ha sottoscritto un accordo valido fino al 30 giugno 2027, che comprende anche un'opzione di prolungamento per un'altra annata.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

L'U.S. Sassuolo Calcio comunica di aver affidato al Sig. Roberto D'aversa la guida tecnica della Prima Squadra fino al 30 giugno 2027. Lo staff tecnico sarà composto da Salvatore Sullo (allenatore in seconda), Marco Piccioni (collaboratore tecnico), Marco Riggio (collaboratore tecnico), Paolo Rongoni (preparatore atletico), Francesco Petrungaro (preparatore atletico), Andrea Rinaldi (preparatore atletico), Simone Vignudelli (preparatore atletico) e Marco Bizzarri (allenatore portieri). Il nuovo allenatore dirigerà nel pomeriggio odierno il suo primo allenamento alla guida dei neroverdi. Roberto D’Aversa torna in una panchina di Serie A dopo l’ultima avventura avvenuta la scorsa stagione subentrando a l’ex tecnico biancoceleste Marco Baroni con il Torino, terminata con il raggiungimento della salvezza ma non con il rinnovo di contratto per l’attuale stagione. Il tecnico è così rimasto senza  squadra per l'inizio di questa stagione, rimanendo inizialmente fermo in attesa della chiamata giusta; l'occasione è arrivata ora con la chiamata del Sassuolo, che ha deciso di affidargli la guida tecnica per dare una svolta al proprio campionato.

#2213. Celtic star’s agonising goal drought inspires ruthless online game

Kasper Hogh’s struggles in front of goal have now inspired an online game where the aim is simple: try to make the Celtic striker score.

The only problem is it appears almost impossible.

Hogh is enduring a torrid dry spell for the Hoops, having failed to find the net in his last 15 appearances. It has now been 1,053 minutes since the £11 million striker last scored, against Kilmarnock back in August.

And someone has decided to make light of his misfortune by creating Hogh’s Hotshots: The Impossible Finisher.

Players take control of Hogh and attempt to fire the ball beyond the goalkeeper, only for an increasingly ridiculous selection of obstacles to get in the way.

Efforts can be saved by the goalkeeper, crash back off the woodwork, or fly harmlessly into row Z. At one stage, Hogh simply falls over while attempting to shoot. Even finding the back of the net does not necessarily guarantee success, with VAR capable of intervening to chalk the goal off.

The Celtic VAR denial you can't 'unsee' as leading ref drops unflinching take

3-man panel split over Celtic VAR flashpoint as key ref claim made

Watch Ex-SPFL boss see red after astonishing rammy with former Premiership star

Things have hardly been going Hogh’s way recently, although the timing of the game is perhaps unfortunate given his improved display against Kilmarnock on Sunday.

Hogh earned Celtic’s Man of the Match award after producing one of his more encouraging performances in recent weeks, impressing with his hold-up and link-up play.

The striker even thought he had finally ended his agonising wait for a goal with a well-taken finish at Celtic Park. His celebrations were cut short, however, when VAR intervened, and the goal was disallowed because of a foul in the build-up.

The drought therefore continues, but Sunday provided genuine encouragement that Hogh could finally be edging closer to ending it.

After 15 games without a goal, Celtic will hope the real-life Hogh proves a lot easier to get scoring than his virtual counterpart.

#2212. ‘Definitely’: EFL expert has say on Birmingham City’s top two chances

Birmingham City are sat top of the Championship table after their first 15 fixtures of the season. BCFC are above Middlesbrough and Stoke City on goal difference, with the likes of Wolves, West Brom and Swansea City also chasing them down.

The Blues are back in action after the international break with an away trip to the Bet365 Stadium to take on Stoke City as they aim to keep their momentum going. They beat Swansea City 2-1 at home last time out after a brace by Jay Stansfield.

Elek reckons the Midlands outfit can keep it up and has said on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “They can definitely stay there. There is no reason why they can’t. We’re not talking about a Championship minnow here. We’re talking about a club who have invested a lot of money in their playing squad. They were the best League One squad vs the level we’ve seen in a long time.”

He added: “The ascent Ipswich and Sunderland have shown, and to an extent Coventry although that took a few more seasons, the pathway is already there.”

Birmingham City came up from League One back in 2025 after they stormed to the title. BCFC then spent the last campaign adapting to life in the Championship and fell short of the play-offs.

The Blues stuck with head coach Chris Davies in the summer though and that decision has worked out well for them. They are rock solid at the back and they have the best defensive record in the division at the moment ahead of West Brom and Southampton.

Christoph Klarer and Phil Neumann have both been excellent at the heart of defence, with Alex Cochrane to the left of them. Dael Fry, who joined in the summer after the end of his contract at Middlesbrough, then provides useful back-up from the bench.

Further up the pitch, Jhon Solis, Paik Seung-ho and Tomoki Iwata inject quality into their midfield department. Stansfield, Liam Millar, Patrick Roberts, Demarai Gray and August Priske are all dangerous attackers and can cause serious issues to opposition defenders.

Birmingham City could do with another striker in the January transfer window. BCFC need some competition for Priske with Luis Vazquez struggling to get to grips with English football.

The Blues would also benefit from another attacking midfielder or winger ahead of the second-half of the season. Their pursuit of Joe Gelhardt in the summer was well documented and someone like him would be ideal, although he won’t leave Hull City.

You could also argue that Davies should bring in another central defender this winter too. If Klarer, Neumann or Fry were to get injured, they would be left pretty short of depth in that area.

Birmingham City are on a roll and will be full of confidence. Coventry City and Hull City showed last season that you don’t need parachute payments to go up.

The Blues need to stay grounded though and can’t get too carried away. Their away defeat at Cardiff City last month proved every single match is tough.

#2209. Rangers 'flying swan' penalty blasted by two top refs as third backs VAR

James Penrice has been compared to a swan flying through the air as three former top referees ran the rule over Rangers’ controversial penalty against St Mirren.

Nick Walsh pointed to the spot after the Light Blues defender went down under a challenge from Samuel Ramos, with VAR allowing the on-field decision to stand.

But the call has split the refereeing experts, with Mark Clattenburg and Bobby Madden unconvinced there was enough in the challenge to warrant a spot-kick, while Dermot Gallagher stressed how difficult it would have been for VAR to overturn Walsh’s decision.

Clattenburg, speaking on the So Near, Yet So VAR podcast, said: “Sometimes the best decisions are the ones you don’t give.

Read more: Celtic star’s agonising goal drought inspires ruthless online game

“What doesn’t help Nick Walsh is the way the Rangers player goes down. It isn’t consistent with the contact.

“When you start seeing the small contact on the foot, there is contact, there is no doubt. But when that contact makes him fly through the air like a swan, then you’ve got to question if there was enough contact to award a penalty kick.

“I don’t believe there is. Again, the best decision is the one you don’t give, so just play on.

“Football is a contact sport. Not every bit of contact is a foul, we have to accept that.

“Penrice’s actions aren’t consistent with the contact on the foot. That is enough for a referee to say, ‘I’ve got a doubt’, and just play on.”

Madden was in agreement with his So Near, Yet So VAR co-host and reckoned Walsh had become too focused on the contact itself.

He said: “I don’t think it is enough contact.

“If you look at it from the referee’s perspective, he is very well placed and he will see Penrice take the touch away from goal.

“He will then see the defender coming in and trying to play the ball, not playing the ball and making contact.

“Again, hyper-focused on this contact, probably not recognising that the reaction from Penrice did not merit the contact he received, and he has awarded a penalty kick very confidently.

“It is very difficult for VAR to intervene because they will look at it and see this contact.

“That’s not enough for a penalty kick. It’s not enough for that reaction and not enough for a penalty kick.”

Former Premier League referee Gallagher offered a different perspective when the incident came under the microscope on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch.

He said: “He couldn’t have a better view than the referee and, what you said, the defender definitely doesn’t get the ball.

“But where the referee is, he’s got the perfect view. There’s the ball, Rangers player plays the ball, he doesn’t.

“It’s very, very hard to go against a referee in that situation, if at all possible. And there’s the touch there.”

MARK CLATTENBURG: NO PENALTY Accepted there was contact but felt it was not enough to justify Penrice’s “fly through the air like a swan” reaction, believing Walsh should have played on.

BOBBY MADDEN: NO PENALTY Felt Walsh became “hyper-focused” on the contact without considering whether Penrice’s reaction matched it, insisting there was not enough in the challenge for a spot-kick.

DERMOT GALLAGHER: VAR RIGHT TO STICK WITH CALL Pointed to Walsh having the “perfect view”, Ramos failing to win the ball and there being contact on Penrice, making it “very, very hard” for VAR to overturn the on-field decision.

Overall: Two against the penalty, with Gallagher backing VAR’s decision not to intervene.

#2208. QPR’s Top 3 players of the 2026/27 season so far, including resurgent 6-goal/assist star

QPR sit 8th in the Championship table with the latest international break upon us. The Hoops have had some patchy form in recent weeks, but they enter the break off the back of a 2-1 win over Lincoln City.

Julien Stephan and co will be pleased with their efforts to date, but there’s room for improvement. The time without league football offers the R’s a chance to put some work in on the training ground, while we can assess the season so far and pick out some standout stars.

In no particular order, we put forward QPR’s top three players of the 2026/27 season so far…

Ronnie Edwards’ fine loan at QPR in the 2024/25 season meant they knew what to expect when he returned permanently earlier this year. He reclaimed a key role swiftly, and the 23-year-old has gone from strength to strength this term.

Used in defensive midfield and centre-back by Stephan, Edwards is one of the Hoops’ most influential players. As per FotMob‘s data, he stands out in possession as he ranks among the Championship’s best centre-backs for successful passes (767), long ball completion rate (62.1%), interceptions (20) and recoveries (65).

His best displays include the big home wins over Swansea City and Derby County, and the 0-0 draw at Charlton Athletic. Edwards has been consistent all season though, proving his star quality at this level.

Throughout his second stint at QPR, Paul Smyth has endured some tough spells. After three years, some may have expected the Northern Irishman to be phased out of the first XI by the likes of Harvey Vale, Karamoko Dembele, Kwame Poku or Koki Saito, but that has not been the case.

Smyth has retained a regular role in Stephan’s side, and it is not hard to see why. The resurgent 29-year-old shows the commitment and endeavour Stephan desires from his attackers, and he’s added more end product to his game with three goals and three assists in his 14 league appearances this season.

He is tied with Richard Kone at the top of the goal contribution charts at Loftus Road and ranks in the top three of Hoops players for big chances created (3), xG on target (2.0) and expected assists (1.6). Smyth has also won three penalties – more than any other player in the Championship (FotMob).

Last but not least is Pierce Charles, whose influence from goalkeeper cannot be overrstated. The Northern Irish prospect arrived as a highly-regarded talent on loan from Manchester City after his Sheffield Wednesday breakthrough, and he has not disappointed.

Charles has work to do with his shot-stopping, as shown by an xG prevented of -2.47 and a save percentage of 67.9%. However, he makes this list because of how his abilities with the ball have changed the way QPR play.

His distribution ability makes Stephan’s side so much more comfortable at the back and they have more routes to the attack thanks to his range of passing. No Championship goalkeeper has made more than his 564 successful passes (FotMob) and he has fantastic numbers in his pass completion rate (77.7%) and long pass accuracy (46.6%).

It has been a real team effort from QPR to start the season in strong fashion. There were some impressive performers overlooked for inclusion here.

Captain Jimmy Dunne has been key with his physical presence and leadership from the back. Midfielder Glen Kamara has made a positive impact since his arrival as well, and if he continues in his recent form, he will be firmly in the player of the season conversation at Loftus Road.

Ilias Chair and Boy Kemper deserve early mentions too, but injuries have limited their involvement compared to others. Kealey Adamson has been one of the most improved players when stepping in at full-back for the R’s.

#2206. Watford hold talks with 48-year-old boss who has been out of work since October 2025

Watford are sat 20th in the Championship table with 15 points from as many games. The Hornets have struggled for any sort of momentum, putting pressure on manager Alessio Dionisi despite the club hierarchy’s reported desire to give the boss more time than some of his predecessors.

Now though, a report from Romanian journalist Emanuel Rose states Watford have held talks with Edward Iordanescu over the managerial position at Vicarage Road. Contact has been described as ‘positive’, but there have not been any concrete English reports that the Championship side are considering a managerial change.

Iordanescu is available having been out of the game since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025. He previously managed Romania’s national team, alongside prestigious clubs such as FCSB and CFR Cluj.

Iordanescu is a 48-year-old coach who started his career in the dugout in 2010 after retiring in 2004. He was only 32 when he was first named as interim manager of Steaua Bucharest, where he stayed as an assistant coach to Ilie Stan until 2012.

He spent short spells in charge of Fortuna Brazi and FCM Targu Mures in Romania before first earning acclaim at Pandurii Targu Jiu, where his work earned him the CSKA Sofia job in Bulgaria. That stint lasted only 12 games though, and Iordanescu would return to his native in spells at Astra Giurgiu, CFR Cluj (x2), Gaz Metan and FCSB.

The rumoured Watford target managed the Romania national side from January 2022 to July 2024, winning 10 of 28 games and leading them to the UEFA Euro 2024 round of 16 before leaving at the end of the tournament.

A return to club football followed at Legia Warsaw in Poland, but they struggled in European and domestic football with Iordanescu criticised for inconsistent team selection, fruitless tactical changes, poor physical output metrics and disenchantment within the squad.

Iordanescu won the Romanian Superliga once and their Super Cup twice, and the same trophy in Poland once. His most used formation is a 4-3-3, but has also deployed his sides in a 4-2-3-1 setup.

As touched on earlier, nothing has been concretely reported by English or local outlets that Watford are planning a change in the dugout. However, rumoured talks with Iordanescu could indicate that they are staying prepared if they do sack Dionisi at the very leasy.

If there is a time to change manager, it is now. The international break offers a chance to get a new boss in and settled before the return to league action.

Iordanescu could be brought in swiftly and given time on the training ground to work with his new squad before club football returns against Sheffield United on November 21st. However, it remains to be seen if anything comes of the links, with managerial speculation never far around the corner at Vicarage Road.

#2205. Michael Carrick ‘pretty clear’ on Man Utd future despite relegation woes

Michael Carrick remains confident in his ability to oversee Manchester United’s resurgence after a “right mixed” three weeks left his team in the relegation zone and the head coach’s future under scrutiny.

The 20-time league champions will spend the November international break in 18th place as their wait to add to August’s solitary Premier League win against Ipswich continued against Aston Villa.

United showed spirit and all too familiar flaws as Sunday’s helter-skelter clash ended in a 4-4 draw after substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in stoppage time following Tuesday’s 3-2 comeback win against Roma.

Carrick insisted afterwards that he would not walk away from a job that looked like it could be taken from him a fortnight ago and the international break provides an opportunity for the club to take stock.

Asked if the two-week pause comes at a good time for the group, the under-fire United boss said: “Yeah, it’s been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you’re looking at the events.

“But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

“Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.

“But as a normal international week is, you know, we’ll have some training. We’ll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we’ll train, and we’ll get ready for the next game.”

The final international break of the year would be a logical time for United to make a change given there is no free midweek until mid-December after returning with a trip to rivals Liverpool on November 22.

The Open to return to historic Scottish venue after 11 years

Hearts set for six-man injury boost as Wouter Vrancken bullish over revival

Hearts crisis or just a bad week, is Vrancken in trouble and has Jamestown failed?

But Carrick is steadfast in his belief that he can lead the embattled side up the standings having seen enough positives since a 4-1 defeat at Como and 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth left his job hanging by a thread.

United failed to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off in a 2-0 loss at Chelsea, before Tuesday’s stirring 3-2 Champions League comeback against Roma was followed by the dramatic Villa draw.

“Goals change games, and you’ve got to deal with it, and it’s part of something we have to improve on drastically,” Carrick said.

“But there’s more than enough. We’re just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times.”

Carrick is far from perfect but has been let down by United’s transfer business in the view of outspoken defender Martinez and the fans who frequently aim chants at director of football Jason Wilcox.

Left-back was among the areas of need and Luke Shaw’s injury has seen Diogo Dalot often deployed there, but frustrations with the United full-back reached boiling point on Sunday as supporters cheered his substitution.

Head coach Carrick, who was unaware of United’s full-back then being hounded as he left the ground, said: “We’ve got to be careful with that, I think.

“I understand the frustration. I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it. We’re all frustrated. We’re all disappointed.

“The players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that. Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions. He’s played left-back. He’s played really well at times.

“He gives a penalty away. He knows that, maybe he can do a little bit better. Alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake.

“But he cares an awful lot, and he’s given everything, so I like what he brings to the team. I like what he brings to the group.”

#2204. 3 players who Middlesbrough should offload in January, including Micah Hamilton

Middlesbrough sit 2nd in the Championship table with the latest international break upon us. It has been a fine campaign for Boro to date, but they won’t be in any mood to rest on their laurels on the pitch or in the transfer market.

Steve Gibson backed Kim Hellberg heavily in the summer with pricey deals for Will Lankshear, Radek Vitek and more. However, there will be more opportunities in the January transfer window, and incomings and outgoings are expected at the Riverside Stadium.

To streamline Hellberg’s squad and make way for new signings, we put forward three players who Middlesbrough should consider offloading in the winter…

Experienced centre-back George Edmundson was lined up for a move away from Middlesbrough late in the summer transfer window, but a deal never materialised. He has not been named in a Championship matchday squad since the opening-day win over Lincoln City and is firmly down the pecking order under Hellberg.

With his contract expiring at the end of the season, the 29-year-old seems bound to leave Boro at some point in 2027. It would be beneficial for him to move on sooner rather than later though, and a winter transfer will allow him to get back to playing.

The powerful centre-back could be a shrewd signing for a team towards the bottom end of the Championship, or in the top six of League One.

Capped by England at U18 and U20 levels, McCabe is among Middlesbrough’s brightest young prospects. However, his progression has stalled somewhat in 2026 off the back of a tough loan at Plymouth Argyle.

The 20-year-old has been back in the U21s setup this season with not one senior appearance made. McCabe turns 21 in January though, so he is at the age where he needs to get more first-team football under his belt.

Given his promise, it seems unlikely that he leaves Teesside on a permanent basis. However, the club must strongly consider sending the young midfielder out on loan to a team where he is a strong tactical fit and will get plenty of opportunities to start.

Last but not least is Micah Hamilton, who is sure to be angling for a chance to kick his career back into life. His two years at Middlesbrough have not brought the opportunities he would have hoped for, but he still has exciting potential to tap into after his emergence at hometown club Manchester City.

The 22-year-old’s contract at the Riverside runs until 2028. But, with the likes of Rokas Pukstas, Myles Peart-Harris, Jeremy Sarmiento and Amario Cozier-Duberry arriving in the attacking midfield and wing positions during the summer, it seems unlikely that Hamilton forces his way into Hellberg’s plans.

Perhaps an impressive loan would change that, but it may be best for all parties if a permanent exit deal is struck in January. Given his high ceiling, there will be clubs further down in the EFL ready to take a chance on Hamilton if the price is right.

#2203. Manchester United player ratings: United failed to win despite advantage

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur returned from the international break with plenty to prove after a disastrous start to the season.

United arrived with just one win, while Tottenham came to Old Trafford without a win.

Both teams had half-chances in the first half but little to show for them. Tottenham had the better chances with chances for Dominic Solanke, Connor Gallagher and Kudus, but none could take advantage of them.

Manchester United came close in the first half to score after Bryan Mbeumo raced towards the goal on a counter-attack to find Amad. He had a difficult shot, and eventually the shot was too weak to cause any damage. The first-half display was met by boos from the Old Trafford crowd at half-time and during the first half as well.

Solanke had another chance at the start of the second half but put it over the top, amid a wrestle with Lisandro Martinez in the six-yard box. It was United, however, who started the second half with promise.

Substitutions by Michael Carrick around the hour mark made the difference as United showed intent before Mbeumo got the goal off Cunha’s low cross. Luke Shaw was at the end of a scuffle with Bentancur, who was shown a red card for headbutting Shaw.

United failed to capitalize on their one-man advantage and seemed to sit on their 1-0 lead, but Solanke punished them with a header to level the game in injury time. The draw left United with just 6 points off their first six games. The result leaves United with their worst start in 40 years.

Lenne Sammens-6          Quiet afternoon for United no.1 till the goal, where he saw the ball go into the back of the net.

Leny Yoro-6       Defensively was fine but offered little upfront. Played out of position, and he showed good defensive awareness on the right back till his substitution.

Harry Maguire-5.5            Was decent in the first half but wasn’t much of an answer to Tottenham going forward in the second half

Lisandro Martinez-5      Took his eyes off the ball, resulting in conceding a late goal off Solanke.

Luke Shaw-6      Went up high on the pitch and remained a threat with his overlapping threat. Was involved in the scuffle that got Bentancur a red card for headbutting.

Kobbie Mainoo-6.5        Brilliant defensive tackle to deny Tottenham in the 68th minute. Remained composed in tight spaces against a physical Tottenham midfield.

Youri Tielemans-6          A decent performance and was solid throughout the minutes he was on the field

Bruno Fernandes-5        Another quiet and disappointing evening for the United captain after he failed to impress on a day he needed to get a result for United.

Amad-6              A positive return from injury, showed plenty of promise on the wing but failed to get past a resolute Tottenham side

Matheus Cunha-7           One of the liveliest options for United going forward. Provided an assist to Mbeumo to put United up front

Bryan Mbeumo-7.5        A brilliant finish off Matheus Cunha’s low ball to put United in front. Was dangerous going forward and denied a second on a counter by Kinsky off a brilliant long ball by Baleba.

Carlos Baleba (58’)-6.5  A decent debut overall for the Cameroon international. He put in a couple of dangerous balls up the field, including a clear ball to Mbeumo on a counter, who was denied by Kinsky.

#2201. Michael Carrick reacts to Man Utd boos after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

#2200. Bryan Mbeumo reacts to Man Utd draw with Tottenham

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bryan Mbeumo admitted Manchester United have work to do after their frustrating 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, despite scoring a superb second-half goal at Old Trafford.

The Cameroon international put Manchester United ahead in the 73rd minute, finishing in the far corner after Matheus Cunha created the opportunity from a low cross. However, Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory, even though Tottenham had been reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card.

Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2).

3 – Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? pic.twitter.com/DuSpvymZfu

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Mbeumo acknowledged that United had taken too long to find their rhythm.

“We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them,” he said.

Mbeumo recognised the threat Tottenham posed and admitted the result was disappointing, particularly given United’s position in the game before Solanke’s late goal.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.”

United have struggled for consistency in the opening weeks of the season, and dropping points after taking the lead will do little to ease the pressure on Carrick. Mbeumo, however, insisted the team must look ahead rather than dwell on the setback.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

Michael Carrick was pleased with Mbeumo’s contribution, highlighting both the quality of his finish and the different roles he has played since joining United.

“Bryan’s done great. It was a fantastic finish again; he’s obviously played different roles for us but we know what he offers,” the United manager said.

“He’s got good quality and obviously the more goals he scores, the better. He’s doing really well for us.”

Mbeumo’s goal was one of the few bright moments in another difficult afternoon for United. Carrick’s team must now find a way to turn things around from here after just six points from six games.

#2198. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”

#2197. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2195. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

#2194. Melvine Malard becomes Chelsea’s leading scorer as FOUR-goal start strengthens her claim to the No.9 role

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Melvine Malard’s Chelsea goals are beginning to provide a persuasive answer to the club’s centre-forward question.

Her opener in Sunday’s 3-0 victory over West Ham took the summer signing to four competitive goals, making her Chelsea’s leading scorer this season.

That total comprises two goals in Champions League qualifying and two in the Women’s Super League.

The circumstances make those contributions particularly useful. Across three scoring appearances, Malard has broken a deadlock, restored a lead and helped Chelsea put difficult matches beyond their opponents.

Three of those goals arrived while Chelsea were level or protecting a one-goal advantage.

That gives the early return significance beyond its size. Malard has repeatedly contributed while there was still a contest to resolve.

Sunday provided the latest example. Chelsea had plenty of possession but needed somebody to turn an opening into a lead.

Turn and finish 💥Melvine Malard finishes for @ChelseaFCW 🔵#BarclaysWSL pic.twitter.com/eicBNrYMYk

According to Chelsea’s official match report, the Blues reached the half-hour mark without a shot on target despite having 64 per cent possession.

Sjoeke Nüsken created the breakthrough by winning possession and finding Malard.

The striker received the ball with her back to goal, held her position, turned and finished into the bottom corner.

It was an important demonstration of what she can offer centrally. Chelsea could find her under pressure and still get a shot away, rather than needing to release her into open space.

Nüsken’s contribution deserves equal recognition. Her pressing created the opportunity that Malard converted.

The sequence offers Bompastor something useful to build on: winning possession higher up the pitch and finding a forward capable of finishing before the opposition recover.

Malard’s first three Chelsea goals came as a substitute.

Her two-goal competitive debut against Real Sociedad immediately demonstrated that capacity to change a match.

Nüsken released her for the goal that restored Chelsea’s lead at 3-2. Ellie Carpenter subsequently supplied her second, extending the advantage to three goals.

The official account of that European victory records two different routes to goal: a run beyond the defence and a finish from a delivery across the box.

Against Birmingham, her alertness produced another valuable contribution. Malard punished hesitation over a backpass to score Chelsea’s second, eight minutes after coming on, as detailed in the club’s match report.

Those appearances give Bompastor flexibility. Malard has already influenced matches when introduced against tiring opponents, while West Ham supplied a scoring return from the starting role.

Chelsea signed Malard from Manchester United on a four-year contract, bringing her back together with a coach who first identified her potential at 14.

Bompastor later coached her in Lyon’s senior side. Their relationship therefore predates this summer’s recruitment by years.

Speaking when Chelsea announced her signing, Malard said:

“My objective is to become better every single day and to win trophies.”

Her next task is sustaining this contribution across a longer run of matches.

Competition remains productive. Aggie Beever-Jones replaced her at West Ham and supplied Maika Hamano’s late goal, giving Bompastor another reason to value both forwards.

Malard’s strongest argument is the range of situations she has already influenced. She has attacked space, finished crosses, punished hesitation and scored with a defender close behind her.

Four goals offer an encouraging early return. The variety behind them gives Chelsea something substantial to develop.

#2193. Colby Donovan concern as Celtic rising star withdraws from Scotland duty

Colby Donovan has been ruled out of Scotland Under-21 duty after becoming a trusted figure under Martin O’Neill at Celtic.

The young defender has been a regular during Alistair Johnston’s absence and played the full 90 minutes of Sunday’s 1-0 Premiership win over Kilmarnock.

Donovan has earned plenty of affection from O’Neill during his breakthrough campaign, but the 20-year-old will now sit out Scotland Under-21s’ upcoming friendlies against Ukraine and the USA.

Tony Docherty’s squad will play both games at Pinatar Arena in Spain, facing Ukraine on Thursday before taking on the USA three days later on Sunday, November 15.

Calum Adamson, currently on loan at Raith Rovers from Rangers, has also withdrawn, with Sam Chambers and Sebastian Lochhead drafted into the squad.

Donovan’s absence comes amid an impressive season at Celtic in which he has already made 21 appearances in all competitions, featuring in their Champions League qualifiers and Europa League campaign.

His emergence had previously earned him recognition at senior international level, with Sebastien Pocognoli including him in his first Scotland squad.

Donovan did not feature in any of the opening four Nations League matches, however, and was not included in the senior group for the double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland during this international break.

Meanwhile, Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka has also withdrawn from international duty, including the Nations League showdown with Scotland.

The 34-year-old suffered a calf problem in the warm-up before Sunderland’s Premier League clash with Chelsea on Sunday, although he was still able to start the game.

#2192. Danny Drinkwater on Chelsea move he ‘could never turn down’

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

Strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

The most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He says the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater said.

One off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day plans back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing big calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar issue. Players who fall outside a manager’s plans rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s plans after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.

#2191. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2190. Keira Walsh adds another Chelsea weapon as former Arsenal target scores THIRD goal of the season

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Keira Walsh is giving Chelsea opponents another decision to make: protect the penalty area or step out to stop her shooting.

Her goal in Sunday’s 3-0 victory at West Ham took her to three for the season across all competitions. Each has come from outside the box.

For a player whose passing helps organise Chelsea’s attacks, that threat adds another way to influence matches. Recent performances show her contributing both to the construction of chances and their finish.

Against Sociedad, Walsh struck from distance after a corner, helping Chelsea complete their passage into the Champions League’s league phase.

The club’s account of that qualifying victory describes a tight encounter in which clear opportunities were limited.

At Manchester United, Lucy Bronze found her near the edge of the box and Walsh drove her finish into the bottom corner.

She also supplied Lauren James’ goal that afternoon, as Chelsea’s match report records. It was a useful illustration of the choices she offers: attempt the finish herself or release somebody closer to goal.

West Ham provided another example of that balance.

Walsh had already struck the post before Alyssa Thompson carried the ball in from the left and found Wieke Kaptein. Kaptein moved it on to Walsh, whose finish gave Chelsea breathing space.

The official report also records an earlier Walsh run down the channel and delivery towards Sjoeke Nüsken.

Her involvement therefore extended beyond waiting for opportunities to shoot. She helped Chelsea approach the penalty area from different positions.

There was a similar reward against Arsenal a week earlier. Walsh’s saved effort fell to Thompson for the only goal, as covered in our report of Chelsea’s derby victory.

That sequence illustrates why a dangerous shot can matter even when the goalkeeper stops it. Chelsea had a runner ready to attack the rebound.

Our assessment is that Walsh’s shooting gives defenders an additional problem. Closing her down can open a passing route; allowing her time leaves the goalkeeper exposed to a player already finding her range.

Walsh has also explained why she feels comfortable alongside Potter.

Speaking after the Arsenal victory in an interview published by Chelsea, she said:

“Lexi is really intelligent. She makes me feel really comfortable when I’m playing next to her.”

Her wider assessment emphasised collective responsibility, with team-mates covering for each other and working to make Chelsea harder to beat.

That matters when assessing midfield influence. Walsh’s freedom to help an attack depends partly on the positioning and decisions of those around her.

Potter subsequently started alongside her in Chelsea’s confirmed team against Lyon, giving their partnership another demanding European assignment.

The encouraging feature is the trust Walsh describes. Bompastor has an experienced organiser working with a younger midfielder whose reading of the game she clearly values.

BBC Sport reported that Barcelona rejected Arsenal’s bid for Walsh in September 2024.

Chelsea completed her signing in January 2025 on a four-and-a-half-year contract. Her official club profile outlines the technical quality and ability to dictate tempo that underpinned that recruitment.

Those qualities remain central to her value. Three early goals strengthen the attacking contribution around them, without establishing that she has changed position or should abandon her deeper responsibilities.

For Bompastor, the opportunity is to preserve that balance: Walsh helping Chelsea progress through midfield, supporting those around her and recognising when the space opens for a finish.
