#2189. Top 9 highest paid English players in the EFL Championship

The Championship has been one of the most entertaining divisions in world football for many years, but in recent times, the league has attracted plenty more attention.

English football's second tier has become a strong breeding ground for talent, be it homegrown or imported, with many star names subsequently going on to ply their trade at the top level, both domestically and on the international stage.

Many of the England squad which reached the FIFA World Cup 2026 semi-final and finished third overall under Thomas Tuchel have enjoyed permanent or loan spells in the Championship, creating a pathway for many current youngsters who are flourishing to do the same in the future.

With that being said, there are also many current high-profile names and clubs residing in the Championship for 2026/27, and Football League World have looked at the nine English players who are ESTIMATED to be receiving the highest wage sums, as per Capology.

In ninth is Burnley's Marcus Edwards, with the former Tottenham Hotspur man earning £50,000 per week.

The 27-year-old's time at Turf Moor has certainly been one of intrigue, as he was a part of Scott Parker's promotion-winning side two years ago, before struggling to make an impact in last season's Premier League.

The Cyprus international winger was also initially omitted from the Clarets' 25-man squad for this season after Deadline Day in September, before being reinstated by former boss, Nicky Hayen, after a four-game absence.

He has since started all three of Fabio Celestini's first matches in charge.

FLW looks at what AI believes will be in the second tier in the year 2050

Kalvin Phillips' recent career path has generated plenty of interest, with the 2020/21 England Player of the Year now in the thick of a second loan spell at Sheffield United from Manchester City.

The experienced midfield player's £42m switch to the Etihad Stadium from Leeds United simply hasn't worked, and despite an underwhelming first stint at Bramall Lane during the second half of last season through suspension and fitness issues, Phillips returned to S2 this summer.

Like Edwards, the 30-year-old is said to be earning £50,000 per week, although it remains to be seen how much of said figure is paid by the Blades.

Max Kilman is the third and final player on this list said to be earning a £50,000 weekly salary, this time with West Ham United.

The Irons parted with £40m two summers ago to secure the defender's signature from Wolves, but it is fair to say that, during his time at the London Stadium in the Premier League, Kilman's reputation with supporters was far from the greatest.

Despite West Ham's shaky start and high-profile managerial change, the 29-year-old has turned around his own individual performance levels and has already chipped in with two goals at the other end of the pitch.

Adam Armstrong has become a guaranteed goalscorer at Championship level over time, and recently marked his 500th career appearance.

Wolves signed the forward from Southampton in January for £7m, but he was unable to aid a lost survival cause under Cesar Peixoto's predecessor, Rob Edwards.

Goals have recently started to flow again for Armstrong, though, who Peixoto will be largely leaning on until January due to Raul Jimenez's well-documented injury, whilst he earns an estimated weekly wage of £65,000.

It is estimated by Capology that Jarrod Bowen earns £75,000 per week as West Ham United captain, but such a figure can certainly be marked with an asterisk given the fact the attacker was the only player at the London Stadium reportedly not hit by a wage reduction after relegation.

The 29-year-old was the subject of intense transfer interest from clubs competing in European football this summer, but agreed to the new deal on July 17th.

The aforementioned contract does include a release clause, though, which will become active if Bowen's current employers do not achieve a first-time promotion under new boss, Scott Parker.

How much danger are West Ham in when it comes to losing Jarrod Bowen? Comment below!

He is joined on that estimated figure by Kyle Walker, who is into his second season with Burnley after leaving Manchester City.

The 36-year-old has won six Premier League titles during his career, but moved to Turf Moor under the aforementioned Parker on a two-year contract after departing the Etihad Stadium.

There was speculation over the former England international's future post-relegation, and it's fair to say his spell in East Lancashire hasn't got any better of late given the club's situation inside the Championship's relegation zone.

Another former England international full-back takes joint-second spot on this list in the form of Kieran Trippier, who earns an estimated £100,000 per week wage.

After leaving Newcastle United this summer, Trippier agreed a pre-contract agreement with Wolves, although this led to immediate jeopardy given the club's decision to replace Edwards with Peixoto in June, shortly after he and the aforementioned Jimenez had signed such deals.

However, the 36-year-old's early-season influence at Molineux hasn't been played down whatsoever, even if he hasn't featured in each and every fixture.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

James Ward-Prowse is another star Championship name who has earned international recognition in the past, and like Trippier, he is said to be earning £100,000 per week after returning to Southampton this summer from West Ham United.

The Hammers paid Saints £30m for his services just three years ago, but alongside loan spells with Nottingham Forest and Burnley, the technically-gifted midfielder fell out of favour under Nuno, meaning his days appeared numbered in E20 this summer.

With Southampton looking to return to the Premier League this season despite a four-point deduction after Spygate, their returning academy graduate has already become a regular at St Mary's once again under Tonda Eckert.

However, one man who isn't favoured by Southampton's head coach is Aaron Ramsdale, despite the fact he is believed to be the Championship's highest-earning Englishman on £120,000 per week.

The 28-year-old signed under Russell Martin in 2025 for £25m, but after being a mainstay in Saints' relegation season, he was loaned out to Newcastle United last term, with the Magpies paying a reported £4m loan fee.

However, Ramsdale's former loan employers opted not to exercise the option-to-buy within said agreement, and he is yet to feature for his current side this season, with Eckert re-signing Daniel Peretz from Bayern Munich on a permanent basis instead.

#2188. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2185. Wolves should be on Sheffield United transfer alert after fresh Bramall Lane update

Wolverhampton Wanderers head into the international break within touching distance of the automatic promotion spots in the Championship, as the Old Gold maintain their strong bid for an immediate return to the Premier League.

Wolves can be satisfied with how things are panning out upon their return to the Championship, as after just under a third of the way through the campaign, the Black Country outfit sit just one point beneath the automatic places.

Level on points with bitter rivals West Bromwich Albion at this stage, only Birmingham City, Middlesbrough, and Stoke City sit above the Old Gold as things stand, as Portuguese boss Cesar Peixoto strengthens his position at the helm at Molineux.

Of course, there is a long way to go yet, and with the two-week international break presenting an opportunity to step back and assess things, Peixoto may be preparing plans for the upcoming January transfer window.

Wolves weren't especially busy in the summer transfer window, as with the likes of Joao Gomes, Tolu Arokodare, Santi Bueno, and Hwang Hee-chan leaving, each of Raul Jimenez, Kieran Trippier, Jordan James, and Rafiki Said arrived.

Joining those aforementioned four through the Molinuex doors was Ivorian left-back Ghislain Konan, joining on a free transfer to provide another option in that area of the pitch for Hugo Bueno.

Bueno has more often than not been preferred there at this stage by Peixoto, though Toti Gomes has recently filled in there when called upon, as Konan has managed just two league appearances thus far.

Looking ahead to the winter window, another option in that position shoudln't be counted out, as Wolves must be on alert to the recent transfer update at Sheffield United.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top nine toughest fanbases in the EFL Championship right now from least to most

Sheffield United, according to Rudy Galetti's Substack, are interested in Lyngby's Belgian left-back Renzo Tytens, as well as Motherwell defender Emmanuel Longelo.

It would appear as though Chris Wilder is preparing to bolster his options in that area of the pitch, despite already having the likes of Harrison Burrows, Rhys Norrington-Davies, and Sam McCallum to choose from.

Burrows has battled with McCallum for a place in Chris Wilder's starting XI over the past couple of years, and the Blades' interest in bringing another player into that area of the pitch ought to be ringing alarm bells for the former Peterborough United defender.

Under contract until the summer of 2028, Sheffield United could be looking to cash in on the 24-year-old whilst they still can, and if they do, Wolves should be the first in line for his signature.

Would you like to see Burrows at your club? How much would it cost to lure him away from Sheffield United? Share your thoughts below!

Wolves certainly have their sights fixed on the automatic promotion spots right now, and are ready to hunt down the teams in front of them.

Anything other than an immediate return to the Premier League would surely be deemed a failure for Wolves, who should be throwing the chequebook at Burrows this winter to boost their promotion bid.

Following relegation to the Championship last season, West Ham have so far struggled to adjust to life back in the second tier.

Nuno Espírito Santo has been dismissed from his role as head coach after six wins, four draws, and three defeats in the league, as former midfielder and fan favourite Parker has since taken his place in the technical area.

Parker will gladly take this two-week break to assess the situation that he has walked into in East London, and may well be disenchanted by some of the transfer business his side conducted over the summer.

It took West Ham a while to get up to speed in the transfer window over the summer, as new head of recruitment Nils Koppen, alongside former boss Nuno, spearheaded recruitment.

As Mateus Fernandes, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Crysencio Summerville, and El Hadji Malick Diouf left the club for lucrative fees, the likes of Edvin Austbo, Joel Piroe, Manor Solomon, and Arne Engels arrived.

However, one of the more low-key outgoings over the summer was that of James Ward-Prowse, who returned to former club Southampton for a fee reported to have been less than £1 million, with the Hammers keen to get his wages off their books.

Ward-Prowse endured a rollercoaster of a spell in East London, as his time with the Hammers was made all the more difficult by Parker's predecessor.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top 25 most demanding fanbases in British football right now

Ward-Prowse, 32, joined West Ham in the summer of 2023 for around £30 million following Southampton's relegation to the Championship, having previously made over 400 appearances for the Saints.

Signed by then-manager David Moyes, Ward-Prowse enjoyed an excellent first campaign with the Hammers, scoring seven and assisting seven in 37 Premier League games.

However, as Moyes left the following summer, his successor, Julen Lopetegui, quickly made it apparent he was no fan of the Englishman, as the midfielder was allowed to join Nottingham Forest on loan, then managed by Nuno.

Ward-Prowse would return to West Ham after just six months at the City Ground under the watch of Graham Potter, but as Nuno replaced the current Sweden men's national team boss in the summer of 2025, the 32-year-old found himself out of the fold with the Hammers once more, even being exiled from training sessions.

In total, Ward-Prowse has made just 12 appearances under Nuno, as the Portuguese head coach, for whatever reason, never took to the midfielder, who would spend the second half of last season on loan at Burnley under a familiar face.

When Parker assesses his current West Ham squad, the former England midfielder will be largely pleased with the current makeup of it, though it won't have taken him long to identify areas with much-needed attention.

Though Engels looks to be an excellent addition in the middle of the park, Parker now has the task of striking the right balance in that area of the pitch, with Divine Mukasa, Tomáš Souček, Soungoutou Magassa, Mohamadou Kante, and Lewis Orford each vying for a place in the starting XI.

The former Fulham, Bournemouth, and Burnley boss is certainly not short of options, though whether he is a fan of any remains to be seen, as what is clear is that he is indeed a fan of Ward-Prowse, having brought the midfielder to Burnley in January 2026.

The Englishman made 14 appearances under Parker across all competitions in less than six months at Turf Moor, more than he has ever made under Nuno, as the new head coach must rue the Portuguese's decision to sell him now.

Parker, meanwhile, must surely regret his side's decision to part ways with the Englishman, especially for such a minimal fee, as there is every chance he could've been one of the first names on the team sheet for the Hammers instead.

#2179. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

#2176. Top 25 EFL Championship goalscorers since the 2004 rebrand

Goalscorers are often the difference between a Championship side merely competing and one capable of going up, which makes them among the most valuable commodities in the game. Football League World have looked at the top 25 since the inception of the division in 2004.

Of course, a reliable striker can turn draws into wins, settle tight games, and provide the consistency required over a gruelling 46-game season. However, the problem for Championship clubs is that when one of those forwards hits the ground running, they do not always get to enjoy the benefits for very long.

A prolific season in the second tier can put a player firmly on the radar of top flight clubs looking for a proven goalscorer, while the alternative is often just as painful for the Championship club when the striker scores enough goals to help fire them to promotion and then faces a new challenge in the top flight.

It is little surprise, then, that centre-forwards regularly command some of the biggest transfer fees and salaries in football. There have been plenty of prolific names in the Championship since the division was rebranded ahead of the 2004/05 season, with some strikers establishing themselves as second-tier specialists and others using it as a springboard towards the Premier League.

Some of the division's most exciting modern goalscorers are not yet eligible for this particular list because they simply have not spent long enough in the Championship. Middlesbrough's Will Lankshear, Wolverhampton Wanderers' Raul Jimenez, West Ham's Taty Castellanos, and Southampton's Cyle Larin are among the forwards currently capable of making their mark, but their Championship stories are only just beginning.

But who has actually scored the most goals since the Championship era began? Including play-off goals as well as goals scored during the regular league season? We have taken a look and ranked the top 25, here.

His Championship career took Martyn Waghorn to a number of clubs, including Leicester City, Ipswich Town, Derby County, and Coventry City. He was particularly effective during his time at Ipswich, where his goals made him one of the division's leading forwards. His 78 goals put him just ahead of Britt Assombalonga and David McGoldrick below him in the standings, but there are the likes of Kieffer Moore and Ben Brereton-Diaz closing in on his tally from the crop of currently active players.

Joel Piroe has established himself as one of the Championship's most reliable modern goalscorers, reaching 78 goals during spells with Swansea City, Leeds United, and now West Ham United. The Dutchman has been particularly prolific in the second tier and remains an active player capable of climbing this list further. Piroe will hope more goals can help the Hammers achieve their ambitions this season, with his 78 goals just ahead of Waghorn on a goal-per-game basis.

Across England's top two divisions, Chris Wood has enjoyed an outstanding career, with his Championship goals coming for the likes of Leicester, Leeds, Millwall, Ipswich, and Birmingham City. His 78 goals match Waghorn's tally as well as Piroe's, but his superior goals-per-minute ratio means he sits higher than both. Wood has not played a minute of Championship football since leaving Leeds for Burnley and has gone on to score 92 goals in the Premier League as well.

One of the Championship's most experienced forwards during the 2000s and early 2010s, Marlon King scored regularly for clubs including Watford, Coventry, and Birmingham. He eventually reached 80 goals in the division, underlining his consistency across a lengthy second-tier career which began prior to the Championship's rebranding. King's physical presence and eye for goal made him a valuable Championship striker for many a year.

Premier League pedigree did not prevent Kevin Phillips from continuing to score at an impressive rate in the Championship. After his famous goalscoring exploits with Sunderland, Phillips found the net regularly for clubs including West Bromwich Albion, Birmingham, Blackpool, Crystal Palace, and Leicester. His 82 Championship goals highlight that his finishing ability remained intact well beyond his top-flight peak and well into his 30s.

During spells with the likes of Watford, Middlesbrough, and Blackburn Rovers, Danny Graham became one of the Championship's most dependable goalscorers. His movement and finishing made him a consistent threat for years, while his goals helped earn him opportunities in the Premier League. Graham's 83 goals leave him inside the division's top 20 scorers since the 2004/05 rebrand.

Peter Whittingham was one of the defining Championship players of his generation, spending much of his career with Cardiff City after an earlier spell at Aston Villa. His left foot, set-piece ability, and eye for goal made him an influential attacking midfielder or winger rather than a conventional striker. His 84 goals are an impressive return for a player operating primarily from midfield. Although he was an attacking player, he is one of only two midfielders on this list.

Dexter Blackstock never scored more than 13 in a season and only hit double figures three times as well, but consistency rather than one spectacular scoring season was the hallmark of his Championship career. He represented clubs including QPR and Nottingham Forest, becoming a familiar figure across the division. Blackstock's 84 goals put him level with Whittingham, although his goals-per-minute record places him slightly better on this particular ranking.

After scoring a few for Newcastle United and then joining Fulham, Aleksandar Mitrovic wasted little time establishing himself as one of the Championship's most fearsome strikers. He scored for Newcastle before his remarkable Fulham spell produced a record-breaking individual season and helped secure promotion. His 85 goals are a remarkable total considering how much of his career has been spent outside the Championship. He has the best goal-per-minute ratio of any player on the list.

FLW have ranked the 10 best EFL Championship stadiums for atmosphere so far in the 2026/27 season.

A remarkably long Championship career saw Cameron Jerome represent clubs including Cardiff, Birmingham, Norwich City, and Derby County. His pace and power made him difficult to contain, while his longevity saw him accumulate 86 goals. Jerome's ability to contribute across multiple clubs, as well as many generations of Championship football, makes his tally particularly impressive.

#2175. Fabrizio Romano shares latest on Martinez contract after explosive rant

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”

He added that Martinez is expected to return to the squad as normal, with the fine considered sufficient punishment for the incident.

“The internal discussion also helped to resolve all the issues. For Man Utd, the case is closed.”

That should bring some immediate clarity to the situation, although questions remain about how the episode could affect Martinez’s longer-term position at Old Trafford.

Romano also pointed towards Martinez’s contract, which expires next summer, with United holding an option to extend it.

“So, let’s see what is going to happen there. For sure, this is the kind of situation that will have an impact on the situation surrounding Lisandro, but we have to see what happens next in terms of future transfers and everything else.”

However, his representatives are said to be open to looking for another move if things do not improve in Madrid.

It seems Arsenal are interested in signing Endrick on loan with a view to making the move permanent. This will give them time to see how he settles into the Premier League.

However, Real Madrid may be in a strong position. They are still loyal to the young player and would prefer to keep him at the Spanish club.

Arsenal will rely on Madrid being more willing to let him go.

The reported interest from Arsenal comes as Arteta looks to strengthen his attacking options.

Endrick would provide variety to an attacking line-up which has been under pressure of late. His age and potential make a loan deal with an option to make the move permanent an attractive option.

There is also positivity from his previous stint with Lyon. He has already been on a loan move from Madrid and has demonstrated that he can make progress when getting regular game time.

Arsenal have previously signed young talents from Real Madrid.

Martin Odegaard came to north London as a young player after failing to make an impact in the first team at Madrid. He then became a key player for Arteta, taking on the role of captain.

Endrick will be hoping to follow a similar trajectory.

There is no suggestion that any deal is near despite Arsenal’s interest.

Endrick remains an important part of Real Madrid’s long-term plans. His representatives are thought to be looking at other options to help his career develop.

This loan deal would provide a solution for all parties. Arsenal would have another attacker to bring in, Endrick would play more regularly and Madrid would still have an interest in his future.

It will also depend on how willing the Spanish giants are to move their stance before January.

For now, Arsenal are in contact with Endrick as they consider a move. The Brazilian’s future may soon become a topic of interest ahead of the winter transfer window.

#2171. ‘It’s wrong’ – Sheffield Wednesday and Barnsley slammed for ticket situation

This article is part of Football League World's 'Terrace Talk' series, which provides personal opinions from our FLW Fan Pundits regarding the latest breaking news, teams, players, managers, potential signings and more…

By the time Sheffield Wednesday travel to Oakwell to face Barnsley on the 20th November, the Owls squad will be hopeful of finding their feet under the guidance of new boss Dave Challinor.

After parting ways with Henrik Pedersen, the Owls moved swiftly to bring the former Stockport County boss to Hillsborough, who took the Hatters from the National League into the third tier in just five seasons.

The 51-year-old will be keen to have further success in the Steel City, taking on massive expectations and pressure that comes with leading such a huge club in English football.

But his reign got off to a very poor start last weekend as they were one of the first upsets in the FA Cup, with Wednesday dumped out of the competition at the first hurdle by losing 2-1 away at League Two outfit Oldham Athletic.

The Owls return to cup action on Wednesday evening by hosting Accrington Stanley in the group stage of the EFL Trophy, while they have another home game this coming weekend in League One as they clash with promotion rivals Plymouth Argyle.

After a meeting with the Pilgrims, it leads into a Yorkshire derby away at Barnsley, with Friday night football originally expecting to host a raucous Oakwell crowd.

However, there are fears now that Oakwell may not be as full and lively due to the club's ticket prices for both home and away supporters.

Barnsley v Sheffield Wednesday is the Friday night football on the 20th November, with Oakwell hosting a Yorkshire derby.

But there’s been criticism aimed at Barnsley for their ticket pricing for the fixture for both home and away fans.

Wednesday announced last week that the Tykes are charging £35 for an adult ticket, with the Owls handed an allocation of 4,810.

Plenty of supporters are bound to be viewing this as extortionate, particularly when the game is being broadcast live on Sky Sports.

Sheffield Wednesday were defeated by League Two opposition in Dave Challinor's first game as manager

Along with the adult ticket pricing, seniors (65+) are charged at £25, young adults (19-21) are also set at £25, while under-19s are £16 and under-14s are set at £10.

So this in mind, FLW’s Sheffield Wednesday fan pundit has given his thoughts over Barnsley’s decision to charge adults £35 a ticket.

Speaking to Football League World, Sheffield Wednesday fan pundit Patrick McKenna has blasted Barnsley for charging £35 per adult ticket for the clash against the Owls, labelling it as ‘wrong’ and a problem in football that keeps on rearing its ugly head.

Patrick told FLW: “To be fair, as Sheffield Wednesday fans, we really can’t say much about club’s charging away fans too much.

“Throughout the Chansiri era, we consistently charged high prices, and away fans had to pay them.

“Now it’s wrong, we charged too much, and it’s wrong when Barnsley are doing this. You see across football high ticket prices, which can’t be justified.

Wednesday fans, how do you feel about Barnsley's decision to charge your travelling fans £35 for an adult ticket? Comment below!

“Unfortunately, as fans, there’s not much we can do. All we can really do is pay the ticket or not go, but we can’t really, as a fanbase, criticise because there would be that hypocrisy on our part.

“Talk to any Wednesday or Barnsley fan, and we’d both be hoping for lower prices, so yeah, it’s disappointing that this sort of thing is still happening in football, but it has done for a long time and, unfortunately, it’s not something that’s going to go away.”

A massive problem with football throughout the country is pricing, with tickets getting more and more unaffordable as the cost of living gets tougher and tougher.

And Barnsley are offering little help to either their own or Sheffield Wednesday supporters through their latest price sting, with some simply unable to pay such hefty prices for a League One standard football match.

In what should have been a fiery cauldron of noise given it’s a local derby, there will be collectively fewer supporters at Oakwell on that Friday evening, with some electing to watch it on TV.

Because of this, supporters from both sides are being driven away from a game that has the potential to turn both Barnsley and Sheffield Wednesday’s seasons around, with the two sides currently enduring slumps that could be snapped out of through a derby day victory.

Unfortunately, these latest ticket hikes in the third tier reinforce the sad state that football is in at the minute, with clubs failing in their duties to make football an affordable escape at any professional level of the game.

#2170. Arsenal news: Arteta’s side secure landmark victory at Anfield

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

In Arsenal news, Arsenal have finally found a way to win at Anfield again. Their latest victory owed as much to defensive discipline as Kai Havertz’s decisive goal.

The Gunners claimed a 1-0 Premier League victory against Liverpool, ending their 14-year wait for victory at the iconic stadium. Declan Rice set up their opener as Havertz put the visitors ahead on the 16th minute.

It was a tough afternoon for Mikel Arteta’s side as they were put under sustained pressure by their opponents. The Reds also created a number of dangerous chances throughout the match, especially in the first half.

Arsenal held their composure, and the backline was calm throughout. David Raya made the crucial interventions to keep the lead safe.

They are now three points ahead at the top of the Premier League after Manchester City lost to Brighton.

While the attack has been a key aspect of Arsenal’s title charge, they were put under pressure defensively at Anfield.

Liverpool came out aggressively after going behind. Virgil van Dijk caused problems from set pieces, and Florian Wirtz hit the crossbar from a free kick.

Raya was quick to block Van Dijk’s dangerous flick on and prevent Alexander Isak from capitalising. However, Alexis Mac Allister did head over the bar as Liverpool looked to level the game.

Arsenal were forced into another stretch as Jurrien Timber blocked well. William Saliba and Gabriel helped to limit Liverpool’s chances.

The stats tell the story of how well the visitors defended. Liverpool had 17 shots but couldn’t get one on target.

Liverpool were unable to create a shot on target for the first time in recorded history (since 2003-04) in a Premier League game at Anfield.

Meanwhile, it was the first time that Arsenal had kept a clean sheet in the Premier League at the ground since September 2012. The result was especially important following their Carabao Cup heartbreak against Fleetwood Town earlier in the week.

Whilst they have made a great defensive stand, Arsenal’s two most influential players in the final third made the difference.

Rice won the turnover, drove down the right and played a low cross into the six-yard box. Havertz made his run to the back post and finished to give Arsenal the early lead.

The goal also takes Havertz to 46 Premier League goals, making him the most prolific German in the competition and overtaking former Manchester City midfielder Ilkay Gündogan.

Rice had a huge influence on the game. His performance in the middle of the park helped Arsenal deal with the intensity of Liverpool, and he was named man of the match.

Christos Tzolis provided an important attacking outlet. His pace created chances to ease pressure on Arsenal. He forced an incredible save from Alisson with a late first-time effort.

The win was Arsenal’s first at Anfield in any competition since September 2012 and their 300th away win in the Premier League.

Arteta’s team have had a stellar start to the season, taking 24 points from nine games. They have also proved they are capable of getting results in tough circumstances.

They will now look ahead to their Champions League game on Wednesday against Slavia Prague and then back to domestic action against Hull City.

Leeds United welcome Manchester United to Elland Road on Sunday, with both sides looking to put a difficult run of results behind them and get their Premier League season on track.

Leeds United suffered a 2-1 defeat away to Arsenal last weekend despite James Justin scoring to put them in front in the 55th minute.

#2167. Arsenal injury news: Eberechi Eze concern emerges as Bukayo Saka awaits scan

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal came out on top in their match against Liverpool. Mikel Arteta admitted they have a new injury concern to deal with after Eberechi Eze was hurt. Bukayo Saka is also still out for the Gunners as they face two more games before the break.

The 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield means they are three points clear at the top of the Premier League. Arteta will need to be careful with his squad ahead of their Champions League clash against Slavia Prague on Wednesday and home game against Hull City.

Eze was a surprise omission from the starting line-up, despite featuring well in recent games.

Arteta later revealed that the England international was suffering from a problem going into the game. He also praised the club’s medical and performance team for getting him fit enough to be included in the travelling party.

There is some light at the end of the tunnel, with Eze being named on the bench. There is uncertainty over whether he will be available for the trip to Prague.

Arsenal will look to train him to see if he can play against Slavia. However, Arteta’s comments suggest that the issue is significant enough that he couldn’t start against Anfield despite his recent form.

There is positive news on Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori. All three were able to overcome their fitness concerns to start the game against Liverpool and play the full 90 minutes.

The availability of these players provides Arteta with more options as he heads into a busy week. However, he will be keen to avoid any unnecessary risk to those that have only just returned to full fitness.

Saka is still the biggest injury concern for Arsenal as he has failed to play for the last three games after suffering a quad injury in the clash against Bayern Munich.

He was forced off after just 10 minutes of the Champions League draw. He will not be available for the fixtures against Slavia Prague and Hull.

There were concerns that Saka may miss up to eight weeks of action. Arteta hasn’t confirmed when he will be back on the pitch.

The Arsenal manager explained earlier that there was a need to scan Saka again to see how the fluid around the injury was behaving. The medical staff will also want to know if there has been any damage to the tendon.

This will give clearer information on when he will be able to return to play. Until then Arsenal will have to plan without one of their most important attacking players.

Another player looking to make his way back to fitness is William Saliba. The defender has not played this season after aggravating a back issue during his time playing for France at the World Cup.

However, he has avoided surgery and has been back in individual outdoor training at the club’s training ground recently. Arteta says there are positive signs that his recovery is going well.

The club plan for an MRI scan to see how he is recovering. They are hoping to get him back in December, but it has not been confirmed by Arsenal.

It would give Arteta a huge boost to his defensive options. For now he will have to keep monitoring his recovery.

They play Slavia Prague on Wednesday and then play Hull at home on Saturday. This gives them two more chances to build up their position ahead of the international break; however, Arteta will have to consider the latest medical reports.

#2166. Nottingham Forest plot move for 'colossal' Birmingham City ace

Birmingham City's ascent to the Championship summit has led to a fresh round of transfer speculation involving German centre-back, Phil Neumann.

According to Sky Deutschland, Nottingham Forest and Fiorentina are casting eyes over the centre-back's strong performances at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

Blues currently top the table on goal difference, ahead of Middlesbrough and Stoke City with 29 points from their first 15 matches, conceding just 14 goals - the Championship's strongest defensive record.

Neumann, unsurprisingly, has been a key aspect of such an improvement in this part of the West Midlands, having endured an indifferent first season in English football after arriving at Birmingham last summer following a pre-contract agreement during his final months with Hannover 96.

Transfer speculation involving the 29-year-old isn't exactly new at this stage, as the 6'3" figure was the subject of reported interest in the previous January window and then again in the summer.

However, it would be an untimely blow for Chris Davies if Neumann was to depart B9 in the coming months as the ambitious club stand a chance of realising their promotion dream.

Neumann has already surpassed the 50-appearance mark for Birmingham, with the imperious defender being an ever-present alongside Christoph Klarer in the early weeks of the season.

Having scored three times in all competitions last season, his brace against Wrexham on August 28th sent Davies' side on their way to the first of eight victories so far, and he has continued to impress defensively.

Registering 181 defensive contributions thus far, as well as a duel success rate of 60.9%, such performance levels have attracted the attention of Forest, who have conceded 13 goals in their first 10 league games under Oliver Glasner and sit 16th in the Premier League.

Birmingham City and Middlesbrough are both plotting shock moves for Leeds United-linked Lorient star Arthur Avom, Football League World understands

Having been linked with Sassuolo in January, the defender has also been monitored by Fiorentina, who are currently 15th in Serie A after 11 games, despite conceding 25 goals in the process.

It has also been claimed that a deal could be struck as early as January for the player, who has never featured at the top level in any of Europe's major footballing nations.

Neumann was recently described as "colossal" by former EFL striker, Sam Parkin, and Birmingham fans will be hoping the defender stays true to his previous words during the summer transfer window.

Indeed, the former German youth international was linked with Hull City and Borussia Mönchengladbach, although a move to either club failed to materialise.

Neumann also distanced himself from such transfer calls, saying: "It’s not on me, my agent is getting these calls but I don’t care.

"My focus is on Birmingham and to do good in the season," he added.

Given his importance to this promotion-chasing Blues side, many supporters have voiced their immediate thoughts on the speculation surrounding Neumann.

With figures of between €5m and €10m mooted, one wrote: "Firstly, he won’t leave this winter, we’re in a promotion push. Secondly you’ve massively undervalued him. Minimum £18 million."

Another Blues fan added: €5m euros. Might send him out on loan for a couple of games for that."

"One of the best defenders in the league, he shouldn't go for anything less than 15m and hopefully if we're up for promotion he'd stay till the end of the season," was another viewpoint adding to the consensus.

This stance was hammered home by the comment: "If anyone thinks Wagner would take £10m I think they are very much mistaken. Put another 5 on and they may get to have a conversation."

"Some crazy figures being quoted in the responses here. Would agree if he was 5 years younger. Would be surprised if he went for anymore than £8m-£10m. Don’t think we need to sell tbh," was another strong reaction.

Some associated with Forest are also not willing to entertain such speculation, with a Reds fan posting: "Utter rubbish. Brum won't sell and he does not get ahead of Cunha, Murillo, Diomande or Milenkovic."

Neumann's contract at St. Andrew's is said to expire in June 2028, meaning in January, the defender will be entering the final 18 months of his deal.

As such, Birmingham will still hold plenty of power when it comes to negotiations, although it remains to be seen whether either Forest or Fiorentina are to press forward with such advances between now and then.

#2163. Arsenal transfer news: Arteta considers January moves for two highly rated attackers

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal could have two ambitious attacking signings in mind for January. Eli Junior Kroupi and Kenan Yildiz are reportedly attracting Mikel Arteta’s attention.

Both players have emerged as potential targets as the Gunners consider further changes to their forward line. However, Arsenal may face a battle to prise either youngster away from their current club.

Kroupi is already familiar with the Premier League after making an impressive start to life at Bournemouth. The forward arrived from Lorient and scored 13 goals in 35 appearances across all competitions during his first season in England.

His development was halted by a broken foot in pre-season which required an operation to fix and kept him out of action for around three months.

The 20-year-old has now returned to the Bournemouth squad and has played as a substitute in their last three games. He will be hoping to get more game time as he gets back into full fitness.

Arsenal were linked with a move for Kroupi in the summer. His return to action has reignited interest in the player. A number of other European clubs also understood to be watching his situation.

Kroupi has attracted interest from a variety of top clubs including Manchester United, Tottenham, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

The French Under-21 international has impressed with his goal scoring in his first campaign in England. At only 20 years old, he has plenty of development to do under an experienced manager like Arteta.

However, Bournemouth are said to be reluctant to let Kroupi leave in January. Selling a bright young forward would leave Marco Rose with a tough decision to make.

It could get even more complicated if Alex Scott is also being seriously pursued. Chelsea and Liverpool are both linked with the midfielder.

Arsenal may therefore struggle to convince the Cherries to part with Kroupi during the winter window.

Another exciting option for Arsenal comes in the form of Juventus winger Yildiz. The winger has been linked with a move to North London for a number of transfer windows. He has once again been in the news recently at the end of the summer.

However, the Turkish international has struggled to get going on this campaign. He has only featured once in Serie A and has failed to feature since he suffered an injury.

Juventus have previously shown little interest in letting him leave. Head coach Luciano Spalletti firmly dismissed the prospect during the summer. Indicating that even an offer worth €100 million would not change the club’s position.

However, things could change next season. There are reports from Italy that Juventus may have to sell their star player if they fail to make the Champions League.

The Turin-based outfit are currently sitting in seventh spot in Serie A after just 10 games and are six points away from the qualifying spots.

This means that if they don’t make it into Europe, then it could put more pressure on Arsenal’s pursuit of Yildiz. It could create more pressure on them to raise funds.

Arsenal had a very busy summer with the addition of Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis, Ezri Konsa, Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier.

But they also missed out on a few big names, such as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez.

Despite this, there is still interest in Kroupi and Yildiz, suggesting that Arteta is still looking to strengthen his attacking options. Both players would bring quality and potential to the squad; however, there are some issues with both.

There are many unknowns surrounding this situation. Bournemouth aren’t keen to sell Kroupi and Juventus aren’t in a great financial position.

This doesn’t mean that either player will definitely be moving to the Emirates but much will depend on what happens at their clubs in the coming months.

#2161. Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg breaks silence on Crystal Palace links

Kim Hellberg is continuing to earn admirers as Middlesbrough's pursuit of promotion to the Premier League toils on, and with new interest emerging from Crystal Palace ahead of Pierre Sage's increasingly-inevitable sacking, the Swede has now made his thoughts clear on a potential switch to Selhurst Park.

Middlesbrough will fancy their chances of successfully avenging last season's heartbreaking last-grasp play-off final defeat to Hull City after enjoying a strong start to the opening months of the 2026/27 Championship campaign, which has seen Hellberg's side lock down second-place heading into the November international break with eight victories, five draws and just two defeats from 15 fixtures to date.

Level on points with both league leaders Birmingham City and third-placed Stoke, Middlesbrough have often appeared the team to beat in the second-tier thus far and will intend on picking up where they left off once they return to action in two weeks' time with a double-header against Bristol City and a fellow promotion rival in Swansea - having endured a slight dip in form during Will Lankshear's injury-enforced absence.

The Teessiders have shown that, under Hellberg's tuition, they are capable of finally ending their top-flight exile and getting over the finish line once and for all, which is exactly why the Riverside Stadium faithful will want nothing more than recent links to Crystal Palace to go away.

Interestingly, though, Hellberg himself has now broken his silence on the speculation in a crucial new development.

Hellberg's exploits on Teesside appear to be gaining wider attention, and a report from Sky Sports on Sunday evening named the hugely-popular 38-year-old as one of seven candidates on Crystal Palace's managerial radar alongside the likes of Sean Dyche, Frank Lampard, Vitor Matos of Swansea and leading contender Thomas Frank.

This update, of course, comes amid the impending sacking of Pierre Sage, which is yet to be formally finalised but seemingly represents an inevitability after the Frenchman left the Eagles rooted to the foot of the top-flight table with just two wins from his opening ten encounters heading into the latest two-week window.

Hellberg has publicly spoken of his dream to manage in the Premier League, but that's precisely where Middlesbrough could be headed on his watch and the Swedish boss has now reacted to links with the likely-soon-to-be-vacancy at Selhurst Park.

Having only been appointed at Boro just under twelve months ago, Hellberg discussed the reported interest with Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen and reiterated his desire to focus on the job at hand with the Championship promotion hopefuls.

Birmingham City and Middlesbrough are both plotting shock moves for Leeds United-linked Lorient star Arthur Avom, Football League World understands

When asked how he feels about speculation linking his services with Palace, he explained: "Absolutely nothing, absolutely nothing.

"It's always nice to be on lists like that, if that's the case - it shows you've done something right. But I think it's mostly just talk, and for me it's all about doing a good job here.

"We actually have a chance to get promoted this year. We feel that there is a chance, but then it's clear that it will be difficult.

"We are one of five, six teams, maybe not the biggest favourites, but behind them I think we have a good chance.

"My focus is here and hopefully we can get up, that would have been fantastic of course."

It's abundantly clear that the entirety of Hellberg's focus is on the task at hand, which is getting Boro back to the promised land at the second time of asking - and they've got a real strong shot of doing just that on his watch.

For a head coach of Hellberg's quality - and we scarcely see that in the Championship, truth be told - it could be easy to be swayed by the opportunity to manage at the highest level.

However, Middlesbrough's own project is attractive, with Steve Gibson rewarding Hellberg with no shortage of financial backing to bolster Boro's squad, and they've only strengthened after sanctioning the big-money departure of Hayden Hackney to Everton over the summer.

Indeed, Boro have one of the Championship's strongest and deepest sides, and from defence to attack, stars such as Adilson Malanda, Aidan Morris and most notably the aforementioned Lankshear are all long-term assets with serious future resale value.

Hellberg has a gifted and high-ceiling squad at his disposal, and missing out on promotion with what he has would undoubtedly represent a failure.

Collect every point to win the round. Don’t let Neil Warnock catch you.

Swipe on the pitch or use the pad to move.

That said, there's no better coach to finally return Boro to the big time and, having only appointed Hellberg after Rob Edwards' contentious and ultimately ill-fated decision to jump ship for Wolves merely months after arriving in the North East, they'll only be pleased and relieved in equal measure to see much more loyalty, dedication and focus from the sought-after Swede.

Make no mistake about it, Middlesbrough won't find a finer opportunity to end their promotion hoodoo as Hellberg continues to kick on with one of the strongest Boro squads we've seen in recent history.

Albeit expensively-assembled, there's no denying the vast quality across Boro's squad. Radek Vitek between the sticks and the likes of Callum Brittain, Neto Borges, Malanda and Ash Phillips provides a second-tier backline stiffer than most, even if Hellberg's emphasis on committing bodies forward and dominating possession in attacking thirds can see the Teessiders occasionally exploited in quick counter-transitions.

You won't find many stronger and more multi-functional midfielders at this level than Middlesbrough's, though, which features Sebastian Berhalter, Riley McGree and Morris - and even versatile French defender Malanda.

The attacking line is just as impressive, and when Hellberg can call upon the joint double-act brilliance of Amario Cozier-Duberry out wide and top-scorer Lankshear alongside Tommy Conway and Jeremy Sarmiento, it's no surprise that only two sides are averaging more goals a game.

Middlesbrough fans, how relieved are you by Kim Hellberg's reaction to Crystal Palace? Are you worried at all that the Swede could leave before the job is done? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Middlesbrough have serious, well-stocked quality in almost every area of the pitch and are a joy to watch at full throttle, and Hellberg himself only knows that all-too-well and won't be willing to part with this talented and exciting squad easily.

Boro, in truth, really should have held their nerve to seal a top-two finish last term, but the opportunity for promotion is even greater now with an improved squad and a route back to the top-flight by the time May rolls around may be exactly what's required to ensure Hellberg's long-term future remains at the Riverside.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2160. Jamie Carragher names Man Utd Star who impressed him against Leeds

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United had a difficult evening once again as they were held to a 1-1 draw at Leeds United. Pressure mounts on Michael Carrick as United have just 7 points from 7 games.

Manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right. However, the visitors couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds United from a corner.

The draw extended United’s frustrating run of results, leaving Michael Carrick still searching for the consistency his side need.

Carragher, though, believes there were positives to take from the trip, particularly one performance at the back.

Jamie Carragher has singled out Harry Maguire for praise after Manchester United drew 1-1 with Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Liverpool defender admitted that picking up a point at Elland Road was not necessarily a bad result in isolation, even if United’s recent form made it feel like a missed opportunity.

“Going away to Leeds is going to be tricky for any team except for Manchester City and Arsenal at the moment,” Carragher said.

“A lot of teams will take a point at Leeds this season but the problem for Manchester United is the results have been so poor that they need to start winning games so it almost feels like two points dropped.”

Carragher then turned his attention to Maguire, who he felt played a major role in keeping United in the game when Leeds began to push for a winner.

“But in isolation, getting a point at Leeds is a decent result. I thought Harry Maguire was fantastic, especially in the second half.”

Leeds United grew into the contest after Calvert-Lewin brought them level, putting United under pressure during the closing stages. Carragher felt Maguire’s efforts in defence helped prevent the visitors from falling apart.

“After Leeds got that goal back there was a stage of the game where it felt like Man United could go under, but Maguire at the back held it together for them. He was fantastic.”

The result may feel like another opportunity missed for Carrick, but Maguire’s performance gave United something positive to take away from Elland Road.

#2158. Arsenal U19s face tough Slavia Prague test in UEFA Youth League

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal’s under-19s face a significant challenge when they travel to Czechia to take on Slavia Prague in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday.

The young Gunners have picked up four points from their first three games and will be hoping to build on that in the league phase. Two wins would definitely help their chances of getting into the knockout stages.

They kicked off their campaign with a win against Napoli and put on a great show in a 3-3 draw against Bayern Munich last month.

Those results have left them 18th in the standings, 16 places below their next opponents. With the top 22 teams progressing to the knockout stages, another positive result could prove important for their qualification hopes.

However, Slavia Prague has made a much stronger start and will provide a difficult examination for David Horseman’s side.

Slavia have won all three of their first games in the UEFA Youth League and are sitting in second place. Just behind Real Madrid on goal difference.

They began well with a 2-1 win against French side Lens. They then went on to beat Sabah 3-0 and then put in another strong display against Fenerbahce.

Despite falling behind in Prague, the players fought back to win the game 3-1. The three wins means Slavia are already past the number of points they scored last season in the league stage.

They also advanced to the knockout stages last time, finishing 20th before they faced Benfica.

Mubarak Suleiman put the team ahead twice, but they were pegged back by two goals in the last 30 minutes as their European run came to an end.

This season they have looked like a much stronger team. With a perfect record, they will be one of the hardest teams that Arsenal will face.

The meeting on Wednesday provides an opportunity for Arsenal to get revenge for their heavy defeat in Prague last season.

The two sides met during the 2025/26 league campaign, with Slavia winning 5-1 at home.

Arsenal were three goals down at the break after an own goal plus goals from Bartosz Szywala and Jakub Kolisek.

O’Neill pulled one back after the break, but the home side had the final word as Suleiman and Matej Kotrba scored in stoppage time.

This loss shows how tough it will be for Horseman’s side. Slavia have already proven their attacking prowess against Arsenal and are playing even better in this campaign.

The young Gunners will have to play much more disciplined if they are to leave Prague with three points.

Arsenal fans can watch the UEFA Youth League clash on Wednesday.

It will be streamed via the Arsenal app and Arsenal.com, with the match taking place at the Sports Centre Radotin.

Updates will also be posted here and on the club’s Academy X page.

A full match report, highlights and post-match interviews with Horseman and one of the young players will be published on Arsenal’s official channels.

With them still in contention to qualify for the knockout stages, Arsenal will be looking to get off to a good start. Slavia’s great early start means they will have to play some of their best football of the tournament.

Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds extended their winless run to six matches in all competitions, leaving United with just seven points from their opening seven Premier League games.

Como have shown more promise. Cesc Fabregas’ side beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe before losing 3-2 to Feyenoord. They returned to winning ways against Fiorentina, claiming a 3-1 victory that moved them up to fifth in Serie A, with 14 points from seven games.

#2155. Ex-Burnley, West Brom & Southampton star Jay Rodriguez names best-ever teammate

Jay Rodriguez announced his retirement last week, leaving many reminiscing over his time at Southampton, where he played a big part in their mini-Golden era in the early 2010s.

The 37-year-old scored goals wherever he went, whether that was at hometown club Burnley, West Brom or Southampton, but his best scoring season in the Premier League came at St Mary's, where he was one of the talismanic players under Mauricio Pochettino in the 2013/14 campaign.

Saints finished eighth that year, and while the Argentine left the club and numerous key players followed suit, they laid the foundations for numerous years on the fringes of, or actually getting into, Europe, and a run to the EFL Cup final in 2017.

Rodriguez scored 15 times that season, partnering with Rickie Lambert, who netted 13, with the likes of Morgan Schneiderlin, Jack Cork and a young James Ward-Prowse breaking through behind them.

But it was someone else in that Saints side whom the former striker proudly states is the best player he ever played with.

Rodriguez appeared on the 'I Had Trials Once' podcast last week to talk through his career, and spoke with Gaz Seddon and Gary Stopforth about that Southampton side, of which he made his solitary England appearance while playing in.

The trio ran through some of the players in that squad, including Nathaniel Clyne, Luke Shaw and Jose Fonte, alongside some of the names mentioned above, and Rodriguez was then asked if any of those stood out as "top" players while playing with them.

"Lallana," the ex-Saints man said, pretty easily. "I always say it in everything; he's the best I've ever played with.

Collect every point to win the round. Don’t let Neil Warnock catch you.

Arrow keys or WASD to move. P to pause, M to mute.

Swipe on the pitch or use the pad to move.

"Everything, technical, tactical, as a captain, he'd kill you if you weren't working hard in training, because he'd be working to his maximum. He's really passionate; he loves football."

Lallana was part of the Saints class who departed to 'bigger' things after that eighth-placed finish in the Premier League in 2013/14. He, Lambert and Dejan Lovren all left for Liverpool, while Luke Shaw went to Manchester United and Calum Chambers signed for Arsenal.

There's little surprise in Rodriguez stating that Lallana was the best footballer he'd ever played with, as the now-retired 38-year-old oozed class all the way from his time in League One with Southampton to the Premier League at Liverpool.

The midfielder was one of the driving forces in Saints' double promotion under Nigel Adkins, scoring 23 and assisting 15 across both League One campaigns and then registering 11 goals and 10 assists in their Championship promotion term in 2011/12.

Even the Premier League didn't seem too large a step-up, and when he moved to Anfield in 2014, he was one of the more important players in the early Jürgen Klopp days after the German boss became Liverpool manager in 2015.

Lallana netted eight and assisted seven in the 2016/17 Premier League campaign, but a hamstring injury the following year saw him miss 31 games. Unfortunately, he could never really get a lengthy run without breaking down after that as a Liverpool player.

Do you think Adam Lallana could have been a major player in Liverpool's recent golden era if not for injury? Let us know in the comments.

At Brighton and Hove Albion, he never played more than 1,600 league minutes in each of his four years there, with his minutes being managed even when he was fit to play, and he retired after a year back at Southampton during their most recent Premier League campaign in 2024/25.

Nearly a decade on from that initial hamstring injury, questions are still being asked regarding what his career could have looked like if he had remained healthy while Liverpool were starting to find their feet under Klopp, en route to becoming one of the best clubs in the World.

Rodriguez retires having been one of the more underrated goalscorers in the EFL over the 14 or so years he was in the limelight.

More often than not, he'd go under the radar towards a double-digit scoring campaign regardless of whether he was in the Championship or the Premier League, with his best year coming at West Brom in 2018/19, where both he and strike partner Dwight Gayle netted over 20 each for a Baggies side who finished in the play-offs.

FLW gets ChatGPT to take a look at the roughest, most intimidating sets of fans in the third tier

Even back in 2022/23, a then-33-year-old Rodriguez netted ten for the Vincent Kompany-led Burnley side en route to the Championship title. From then, injuries and a place further down the pecking order stopped him from making much of an impact, both at Turf Moor and then at Wrexham.

Now the boots are hung up, it's fun to look back on some of the squads he was part of, but no doubt that early Southampton side in the Premier League with Adam Lallana pulling the strings in the midfield was the most entertaining.

Arsenal have received a significant boost with William Saliba returning to first-team training. He’s spent almost four months out with a back injury.

The French international was seen returning to training on the pitch. Sparking hope that he could be back in action soon for Mikel Arteta.

Saliba has been sidelined since he suffered the injury in France’s 2-0 semi-final defeat to Spain. The defender was forced off after only 30 minutes after playing the full 90 in his previous five starts at the tournament.

The player was confirmed by Arsenal to be sidelined for a lengthy period of time in July. He did not require surgery, meaning he can begin working back into action.

His latest progress comes at an important point in Arsenal’s season, with several major fixtures approaching.

The 25-year-old has travelled to the Czech Republic with Arsenal’s squad to face Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba had played for 45 minutes in a behind-closed-moors game last week as part of his rehab.

He then returned to full first team training on Tuesday, providing another defensive option for the club.

Arteta spoke ahead of the game against Slavia Prague. He said that Saliba is happy with his recovery and is at a point where he will be used if needed.

The Arsenal manager has not confirmed if the Frenchman will be involved tonight.

Saliba has not played in a competitive game since losing to Spain in the World Cup semi-final for France. So it will be his first involvement in a competitive game since the summer.

Arsenal have coped well with Saliba’s absence.

Gabriel initially partnered Cristhian Mosquera at centre-back before the Spaniard suffered an ankle injury. This allowed Ezri Konsa to come into the starting line-up.

Ezri Konsa settled into a partnership with the Brazilian. He joined from Aston Villa for £51 million in the summer.

The partnership has helped the Gunners to have the best defensive record in the Premier League. Having only conceded 5 goals in their first 9 games.

His return to training is a major step in his road to full fitness, but it remains to be seen if he will play against Slavia Prague tonight.

#2153. Slavia Prague 1-2 Arsenal: Madueke and Gyokeres fire Gunners to Champions League victory

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal moved up to third in the Champions League table after beating Slavia Prague 2-1 at the Fortuna Arena.

Noni Madueke opened the scoring after nine minutes, finishing calmly after Viktor Gyokeres sent him through on goal.

The Swedish striker then doubled Arsenal’s advantage with an excellent finish in the 38th minute. However, a much stronger second-half performance from Slavia made for an uncomfortable finish.

Wiktor Nowak scored a late goal to put pressure on the Gunners. They held on to take all three points.

Mikel Arteta made six changes from the Liverpool win on Sunday. William Saliba returns to the squad after his back injury.

The defender was left on the bench, with Ezri Konsa playing alongside Gabriel Magalhães in central defence.

Arsenal started brightly and took control of the game when they won the long ball forward. Gyokeres beat his man and found Madueke with a clever through ball.

The winger used his pace to get into the penalty area before sliding his finish through goalkeeper Nazar Domchak’s legs.

Arsenal continued to create chances, with Mikel Merino going close on several occasions. Domchak also produced an important save to deny the midfielder from close range.

Merino eventually helped Arsenal extend their lead. After winning possession in the Slavia half, Declan Rice found Gyokeres, who exchanged passes with the Spaniard before curling a superb finish into the far corner.

The visitors could have added a third before the break. Gabriel’s header from a corner was cleared off the line.

Arsenal appeared to be in control at half-time.

But Slavia upped the tempo and started to create more space, forcing Arsenal into a defensive stance. Early on, Oskar Kubiak fired a long-range shot, forcing David Raya to push it away.

Arteta got increasingly frustrated as Arsenal struggled to hold on to the ball and dominate the midfield.

They tried to keep pressing, but Arsenal struggled to create much at the other end. Madueke did get into a good position to shoot from an angle but didn’t have enough power to cause any problems for Domchak.

Slavia were denied a goal when Gabriel headed the ball away from the goal line. Raya made a brilliant stop to keep the shot out while the penalty area was crowded.

The Arsenal keeper made another stunning save as Kubiak powered a header from a cross. Raya deflected the ball onto the post to keep his team ahead by two goals.

Slavia scored their breakthrough goal in the 90th minute after David Jurasek played a low cross from the left. Nowak was able to run into the box to score past Raya.

It created a nervy few minutes of added time as Arsenal had to defend their lead.

Slavia could find no way back into the game as Stepan Chaloupek headed wide and Mikulas Konecny threatened in the dying moments, but his effort lacked confidence as Raya made light work of saving.

Arsenal secured their third win in their last four Champions League games to move to 10 points and into third place in the group stage.

The Gunners have now gone unbeaten in their last ten Champions League away games to set a new club record.

However, Arteta will be looking for a much better display from his side when they resume action in the Premier League against Hull City on Saturday.
