#2126. Blackburn Rovers 2- 1 West Ham United | The morning after

Scott Parker’s words at full time pretty much summed up the remainder of this Championship season for West Ham United following the side’s first away defeat of the campaign. The new manager bounce failed to materialise as his squad thew away chance after chance against their solid opponents who twice capitalised on the now-traditional lacklustre Irons’ defending.

Speaking after the game to BBC Radio London, a hoarse Hammers head coach declared :

Not only at Ewood Park, but in the 31 remaining games of this season. A six point gap between the Hammers in ninth and the league leaders is not yet insurmountable. But it is, certainly, a mountain to climb for Parker to turn West Ham’s dreadfully mediocre-looking squad into Championship contenders.

With so many leaks, it is difficult to know which hole to plug first in the slowly sinking good ship West Ham United. Goalkeeper, defence, midfield, attack – all are areas crying out for urgent post-Nuno repair.. But none are yet beyond salvage.

A tough watch – Scott Parker will have learned a lot about his West Ham squad

As many have commented, though, it’s going to be a long season.

Right now, half a season of the dour, drab, boring but solid wins for which Scott Parker received so much criticism from his time at Burnley would be pretty well received in east London.

Usually we curse the international break but I have a feeling this time around it comes as a huge relief to the manager, the squad and supporters, for very different reasons. Amongst supporters, optimism will no doubt resurface at some stage during the next fortnight as we convince ourselves that if nothing else, we have the right man for the job at the helm.

Whatever Scott Parker is getting paid, if he somehow manages to transform this group into his trademark mean, lean, tough side capable of grinding out one-nil victories week in, week out, frankly he’ll be worth every penny.

#2125. Chelsea news: Stewart departure, Scott interest and Bournemouth preparations

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

#2124. Atletico Madrid eye January move for Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Atletico Madrid are looking to make an ambitious January swoop for Martin Zubimendi after the Arsenal midfielder failed to convince Mikel Arteta to give him a regular starting spot.

The Spain international has started all seven of his Premier League appearances this season, coming off the bench. This has reportedly caught the eye of Diego Simeone, who wants to bolster his midfield in the winter window.

Atletico have marked Zubimendi as a possible target, according to Spanish radio station RNE via SPORT. Sporting director Mateu Alemany feels that there is still more to do with Simeone’s squad despite big investments in new players this summer.

If Zubimendi’s situation fails to improve at Arsenal, he could become one of the most wanted signings of January.

Zubimendi played a major role in Arsenal’s Premier League title-winning campaign last season. He made 34 league starts, scoring five goals and providing one assist.

He played a key role in the club’s run to the Champions League final. Since then Arsenal’s midfield has changed.

Injuries have hampered his campaign, but Myles Lewis-Skelly has returned to the midfield, and Bruno Guimaraes joined in the summer.

The 27-year-old has also expressed frustration at the lack of playing opportunities available to him. He was signed for £60 million from Real Sociedad to Arsenal just 18 months ago and has three-and-a-half years left on his contract.

Any move to Atletico would be a battle. Real Madrid are also reportedly fans of the midfielder, and he has also been linked with a move to Chelsea in recent months.

Atletico are keen to bring Zubimendi in alongside Pablo Barrios in central midfield.

It would be a dream combination for Simeone, and the Spanish club are willing to fund any move.

Another option could see him involved in a deal for Julian Alvarez. There are currently no talks about a potential swap deal.

Arteta has previously played down concerns about Zubimendi’s importance to Arsenal. Earlier this month, he highlighted the midfielder’s commitment and suggested injuries had affected his opportunities.

The Arsenal manager also made clear that Zubimendi would have chances to play, but would need to take them when they arrived.

That leaves the midfielder with an opportunity to work his way back into Arteta’s plans. However, Atletico’s reported interest could add another dimension to his situation as January approaches.

#2123. “Erased” – Media explanation for one star’s waning at West Ham United

West Ham’s Nuno- divided squad was rallied midweek by new manager Scott Parker with his declaration that the slate had been wiped clean and that everyone had a chance to impress. Indeed as if to prove the point his first match day squad included Soungoutou Magassa, one of the summer want-aways who didn’t get his way.

Although the French midfielder was understandably rusty and hooked at half time, Parker had proved his point. Images of the head coach in training alongside-even- Maxi Cornet showed nobody is beyond redemption in the Coach’s search for the right eleven.

However, anxious voices across the Atlantic continue to berate West Ham for ruining the career of Mexico’s national team captain Edson Alvarez.

Few in Central America seem able to understand el Machin’s fall from grace, despite both injury and scandal dogging the midfielder during the summer. Rather than accepting that the West Ham management simply don’t rate their skipper, the understandably patriotic local media indulge themselves in all manner of excuses for their star’s waning in east London.

Edson Alvarez pictured back in training in Parker’s pre-Blackburn session.

“91 days in oblivion, with Alvarez still erased from West Ham.

#2121. Arsenal’s Havertz penalty controversy sparks fresh call for change to football laws

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal’s controversial penalty claim against Hull City has raised new questions about how the offside rule is interpreted in football.

Former Premier League official Dermot Gallagher believes that whilst he understands why the officials made the decision, the result would have been different under the current rules.

Speaking on Ref Watch on Sky Sports, Gallagher said that the holding should have been the main focus of the incident involving Kai Havertz and Hull defender Nobel Mendy.

His comments have increased criticism of referee Farai Hallam and VAR official Michael Oliver. However, Gallagher also feels that the language used in the laws needs to be addressed to avoid this issue in the future.

The incident happened shortly before half-time during Arsenal’s 1-0 victory over Hull at the Emirates Stadium.

Mendy pulled Havertz’s shirt inside the penalty area, prompting VAR to recommend an on-field review. Hallam subsequently confirmed that the Hull defender had committed a holding offence.

However, he ruled that Havertz was in an offside position and awarded Hull a free-kick.

Gallagher believes that was incorrect under the laws of the game. He explained that being in an offside position does not automatically constitute an offence.

The player must be involved in play before the referee can give a penalty. In this instance, Havertz had not tried to play the ball or challenge an opponent before being pulled back by Mendy.

This means that the player was held first, so a penalty should have been given to Arsenal.

Gallagher said that the AR had first raised their flag for offside. He said that it was a great process with VAR, but the initial decision could have affected the outcome.

He recognised why the decision was made even though he felt Arsenal should have been awarded the penalty.

In terms of common sense, he said it does not look right to award the penalty, as Havertz was in an offside position and couldn’t legally contest for the ball.

But he emphasised that the officials must strictly enforce the laws of the game. Gallagher thinks there is some grey space here which can be addressed by having more specific wording.

This could be crucial in these types of situations as the difference between being in an offside position and committing an offside offence can have a big effect on whether a penalty is awarded.

It’s a small comfort for Arsenal after missing the chance to take the lead from the spot. But Martin Odegaard did eventually score the winner in the 72nd minute to give Mikel Arteta’s men three points.

The incident has exposed a wider problem for referees. Until the laws provide clearer guidance, similar decisions could continue to generate controversy.

#2120. The extreme lengths Scott Brown took to avoid being recognised at the darts

Scott Brown has revealed he once attended the darts dressed as a Minion to avoid being recognised.

The Celtic great made the hilarious admission after swapping the football pitch for the oche to take on former European champion Ross Smith at an exhibition event in Edinburgh.

Brown even had his iconic No.8 on the back of a specially-made darts shirt as he went up against Smith. The former Scotland international was handed a sizeable advantage, beginning on 501 while Smith started on 1001, but he was unable to pull off an upset.

Ahead of taking to the stage, Brown admitted he was a big darts fan and revealed the lengths he had previously gone to in order to enjoy an event without attracting attention. He said: “I have been to the darts before dressed up as a Minion; nobody ever knew I was there!

“I really do enjoy the darts. My wee brother is coming along as well, and he enjoys the darts so he’ll be buzzing that I get beat on stage. Playing in front of 60 or 70,000 is OK when I know I can control the ball and pass it, make a tackle and stuff.

Colby Donovan concern as Celtic rising star withdraws from Scotland duty

Why Jota was subbed at half-time for Celtic as O'Neill explains decision

Torreense boss prepares for Celtic 'fight' after both mount Europa League comebacks

“I can’t really judge my darts quality, shall I say. Standing in front of 1,000 people, if I miss the board they’ll be delighted. If I hit the board I will be delighted.”

Brown also revealed his admiration for the elite players who regularly cope with the pressure of performing on stage. The Celtic hero is friends with World Cup winner John Henderson and admitted seeing top players up close gave him an appreciation for the hours of practice required.

He added: “See, when they stand up there with nerves in front of people, I understand the pressure they are under and how well they play. The experience and practice they put in, as well as standing in front of a dartboard, some people might see it as draining. But some really, really enjoy that.

“The ones that stand there and practice are the reason they are world champions, and they are up there in the top 10.”

And despite his love of darts, Brown was not prepared to trade his haul of football medals for success at the oche. He joked: “I’d love to say it would take over them all.

"No. If I get down to just a double, I will be delighted. I cannae remember the last time I hit a double.”

#2119. West Ham fans’ furious reaction raises an uncomfortable question

As the Hammers subsided to their first away defeat in the Championship, long suffering supporters, who’d undertaken the 480 mile round trip to be served up a pretty spineless team performance, decided to let their team have it with both barrels.

After last week’s displeasure culminating an Hammers fans singing ‘sacked in the morning’ to their own manager, this weekend brought the players into the crosshairs as the next logical target for their ire.

..With Nuno Espirito Santo out of the job and with Scott Parker just 72 hours in, the 7,500+ travelling fans turned on their stars.

Under no illusions after the result – and the away fans’ response – yesterday: Scott Parker

..As well as booing their own goal keeper pretty much throughout, if the reports on the radio were correct.

Traditionalists will likely be aghast at the thought of fans undermining their own team in this manner, whilst those who participated no doubt feel it was the only way to show their contempt for the perceived lack of commitment and effort which those eleven representatives  of the Claret and Blue heritage displayed.

Not to mention the hundreds of pounds it costs each supporter, every game, merely to arrive at the turnstiles in support of our club. But is it the ‘right’ thing to do?

For me – it’s a no. I started attending games with my son when he was ten years old and however bad it got (it was pretty dire in that season of 2003-4) we never left early, never booed our own players (Luis Boa Morte excepted, I must confess to once letting my frustration with his indolence bubble over) and always, always applauded those who’d put in a shift, regardless of outcome. And I’d not even heard ‘you’re not fit to wear the shirt‘ sung by West Ham fans in my couple of decades’ worth of attending games.

I just don’t see it helping team morale or positively influencing the final outcome. Which is, after all, the point of ‘supporters’.

Giving ‘The Sun’ another gleeful headline to point out our sufferings sticks in my throat too.

But don’t get me wrong, each has absolutely the right to their own response. Just don’t see it helping is all.

#2118. David Raya names Arsenal teammate as dressing room’s worst DJ in revealing teammate verdict

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

David Raya has offered a glimpse into the lighter side of Arsenal’s dressing room. He’s revealed which teammates make the most noise, take training too seriously and have the worst taste in music.

#2117. “He’s Got The Yips” Mads Hermansen’s West Ham Nightmare Goes Beyond Bad Form

There is a phenomenon in sport known as the yips. It’s a condition which seems to affect previously capable sportsmen, psychologically blocking them from performing even the simplest of tasks. In darts, it can become difficult to release the dart from the hand, while in golf it can make putting almost impossible.

In essence, you’re frozen, seemingly unable to perform a task which should have become second nature. And it was during Blackburn Rovers’ second goal against West Ham yesterday, when I watched Mads Hermansen fail to dive, that I found myself wondering whether this goalkeeper has developed the footballing equivalent of the yips.

It wasn’t just that goal, of course. The first was equally concerning, when Ezra Mayers was beaten down the flank and the ball was crossed into the penalty area. The situation required some kind of intervention from Hermansen, but there was none. No punch, no parry, no save. Just indecision and a complete lack of intervention.

Unfortunately, this apparent hesitation has permeated Hermansen’s game recently and it’s hard not to conclude that he’s got the yips. There have been occasions when he has looked like little more than a bystander as goals have flown past him, sometimes appearing rooted to the spot or simply falling over rather than making a convincing attempt to save the ball.

The statistics are equally worrying. Based on the match figures we’ve examined, Hermansen has saved just 20% of the shots on target he has faced over West Ham’s last three Championship matches, conceding eight goals from ten attempts on target.

That’s an extraordinary return for a goalkeeper at any level, let alone one playing for a club with West Ham’s promotion ambitions. And while defenders must accept their share of the responsibility, the goalkeeper ultimately has to provide some resistance when opponents get a shot away.

The warning signs were already there before Cardiff, and his latest performance has only increased my concerns. I don’t know whether Hermansen is suffering from anything resembling the yips, but from watching him, I do wonder whether his confidence has deteriorated to the point where instinctive reactions are being replaced by hesitation.

This has become a huge problem, and one Scott Parker needs to address immediately. As things stand, I would have more confidence in either Alphonse Areola or Finlay Herrick than a goalkeeper who currently appears unable to make the saves West Ham desperately need.

Areola is an experienced international goalkeeper whom Parker already knows from their time together at Fulham. I thought he deserved his opportunity against Blackburn, and nothing I witnessed yesterday has changed my mind.

Hermansen’s performance was among the biggest disappointments in our Blackburn player ratings, and continuing to select him simply because he was previously considered first choice doesn’t make much sense when his performances have deteriorated so badly.

Clearly, there is a bigger issue to address in January, when West Ham will have another opportunity to examine their goalkeeping options. But we’ve only just entered November, and there are still two months and a hell of a lot of fixtures to negotiate before the transfer window opens.

That’s an awful lot of potential points to lose while waiting for a goalkeeper to rediscover his confidence. Parker has an international break in which to make some important decisions, and I would suggest the identity of his first-choice goalkeeper should be very near the top of that list.

#2116. Scotland striker gets ‘something different’ backing in selection battle

Former Scotland striker Kris Boyd has backed Che Adams to resume leading the line for his country.

The Tornio forward missed Sebastien Pocognoli’s first camp through injury but is back for the Nations League finale against North Macedonia and Switzerland after netting four Serie A goals this season.

Adams has fresh competition in Oli McBurnie, Robbie Ure and Kieron Bowie. But with 13 goals in 50 caps, Boyd believes the 30-year-old’s experience will be crucial.

“I think Che Adams will come back in,” Boyd said. “If you speak to Steve Clarke, he’ll say Che was one of the biggest reasons why they were able to have the success they did.

“It’s not a coincidence that John McGinn and Scott McTominay’s better performances were when Che Adams was up front because he’ll work his socks off for the team. He’s a threat and he can score goals.

“It’s difficult being that number nine for Scotland because there’s so much more asked of you than just scoring goals, and I think Che Adams does that.

“It will do Robbie Ure and Bowie a lot of good. Going into the last block of fixtures for Scotland, a lot of pressure was on the youngsters because all the chat had been around trying to get a lot of younger ones into the group.

“But to actually stand back and watch one of the experienced players who has been there and done it operate will do them a world of good.

“Oli McBurnie worked ever so hard in the last four games. But I feel as if there’s just something different about Che Adams.

“We can’t ignore the fact that Scotland have been to three of the last four competitions and he has been the striker.

#2115. Parker’s words prove he has so much more to offer than his predecessor | West Ham News

West Ham fans may have voiced their fury as the side slid one place further down the table after a poor run of results, but at least in Scott Parker the Hammers have a manager who understands how it really, really feels to have to witness that dross.

Unlike his predecessor Nuno Espírito Santo, Parker seems to have the ability to connect with the fan base and offer real empathy – along with hope that he will at least, work his nuts off to see a turnaround.

Nuno Espirito Santo was reduced to the same platitudes, the same apologies, but with the sense that it was just for the cameras and that he’d shrug his shoulders as soon as the interview was over, leaving someone else to fix the chaos in the dressing room and on the training pitch. West Ham’s training videos usually showed an assistant taking training, with Nuno either passive or absent entirely.

Even after a year Nuno struggled to convince fans that his ‘concern’ was heartfelt.

Parker has already surpassed his predecessor in terms of being ‘present’. Both his pronouncements and his actions – such as his first-game, half time team talk demonstrate his ability to wear his heart on his sleeve.

His words reported yesterday by footballleagueworld.co.uk do suggest, unlike his predecessor, that he’s genuinely hurting, along with the rest of us:

“Sounding somewhat hoarse after his team’s 2-1 defeat at Blackburn, Scott Parker spoke after the matchabout his disappointment at the result. Parker said that he’d talked about his team’s need to get a result from this match, even if it wasn’t playing the sort of football that he want his team to play.

He had sympathy for West Ham supporters, saying that he “wanted to get three points” for them, adding that, “What I can say is that I’m fully committed here, and I understand the pain, I understand where the fan base are.”

Parker added that he understands that the unhappiness of fans isn’t entirely a response to recent performances alone, saying that, “That’s not just this season, it’s come over a little bit of time.”

And he admitted that he was also hurting from this result: “I think everyone’s hurting here, and tonight I’m hurting because I understand that the only way we can change things is winning”

And it matters. In these dark days for the football club, mid table in the second division, leadership is what will unite team and supporters to operate together and hopefully pull the club out of its slide. Leadership doesn’t always yell, ( he’s done that too), sometimes it merely shows understanding and empathy whilst demanding better.

#2113. Ex-Man United star Clayton Blackmore is forced to apologise for encouraging Mason Greenwood to 'come home to us' after winger beat Liverpool with Fenerbahce

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 13:06 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 13:28 EST, 5 November 2026

Former Manchester United footballer Clayton Blackmore has apologised after being criticised on social media for asking Mason Greenwood to 'come home' to Old Trafford.

Greenwood, 25, played a pivotal role for Fenerbahce during their 3-2 victory over Manchester United's archrivals Liverpool in the Champions League on Wednesday, scoring the Turkish giants' first-half equaliser.

The English forward broke through the ranks as a youngster at Manchester United and looked destined to become a key long-term player, but his career spiralled after he was arrested and charged in 2022 with suspected attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault causing actual bodily harm.

Although those charges were subsequently dropped by the Crown Prosecution Service in February 2023, United decided Greenwood could not continue to ply his trade at Old Trafford after undertaking an internal six-month investigation.

Since his exit, which came after disgruntled Manchester United supporters groups heaped pressure on the club to cut ties with the forward, Greenwood has represented Spanish club Getafe on loan, French giants Marseille and Turkish side Fenerbahce, who he joined this summer for a reported €39million (£33.27million).

Blackmore, who played for Manchester United between 1982 and 1994, was met with backlash on Thursday after he heaped praise on Greenwood for his role in Fenerbahce's 3-2 win over Liverpool.

Mason Greenwood (centre) celebrates after scoring in Fenerbahce's 3-2 win over Liverpool

Former Man United star Clayton Blackmore pleaded for Grenwood to 'come home to us'

The 62-year-old Welshman apologised after his post was met with a furious backlash online

Greenwood's Manchester United career ended after he was charged with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault causing actual bodily harm in 2022

'Well done Mason Greenwood beating Liverpool. Come home to us please,' the Welshman, 62, posted on X.

Two hours later, after receiving a slew of disparaging comments on the platform, he said: 'Sorry I've offended anyone but I heard he had been cleared of any wrongdoing I apologise to everyone I've upset with my comments like I said I thought he had been cleared of everything and he’s had a baby with his girlfriend. Big sorry.'

Blackmore had previously come under fire for expressing his sadness that both Greenwood and Angel Gomes, another former English prodigy who was sold to Lille by Manchester United in 2020, no longer play for the club.

When the duo were both playing at Marseille last season, Blackmore said on X: 'Good to see Angel Gomez and Mason Greenwood score Marseille in first 26 mins. Sad they're not still at United.'

After landing himself in hot water with the post, he clarified to those commenting: 'Sorry I understand what you're saying but sometimes everything you hear is not always the truth why did his girlfriend stay with him I'm just looking at the football side.'

He later doubled down and wrote: 'Sorry didn't see or hear any of that I will do my home work next time just looking at it from the football side sorry if I've offended anyone especially his girlfriend and her family.'

While there was noisy resistance to Greenwood joining Marseille in the summer of 2025, he found no such opposition in Turkey, where one prominent journalist claimed 95 per cent of the population would not know or care about his past.

He didn't face any questions about the dropped charges or his public image in his first press conference and outside of brief post-match comments, has not conducted any interviews of note.

Greenwood has been hiding from the limelight a record signing would usually bask in, especially in the football-crazed city of Istanbul.

He found a home in a district called Sarıyer, a favourite among footballers, who largely live in gated communities.

Greenwood is said to count team-mates N'Golo Kante and Marco Asensio as neighbours and was seen in a rare online post after securing his new home, posing with the all-female team of estate agents who helped him with the purchase.

The former United starlet completed his move to Turkish giants Fenerbahce in the summer

Blackmore had previously come under fire for expressing his sadness at Greenwood leaving

Since the big-money move, Greenwood has only posted a handful of times on his Instagram profile, all of which were generic action shots after matches.

His latest offering came after Fenerbahce's stunning win over Liverpool, as he posted a gallery of photographs celebrating in the club's yellow and black jersey.

His partner, Harriet, 26, is also selective with how much she shares from their new life.

She only has four posts in total, with around 20 photos in each 'round-up', offering a glimpse into the high-life, though Greenwood himself only appears twice.

One of the images is of him looking exhausted in hospital at the birth of their second daughter in 2023 and another shows him holding hands with their eldest, Summer, who is three.

In fact, there are some positive signs – Ezra Mayers, as we wrote elsewhere this morning- gives us all cause for optimism.

I’d wager that another starter against Blackburn, Edvin Austbø is perhaps wondering about now what kind of hell he has signed up for as one of the Hammers’ youngest summer recruits.

However his is another fledgling career that looks to be hugely promising. Against Blackburn, the young winger looked prepared to take on and beat players in a way that his more seasoned colleague Manor Solomon appears to have forgotten.

Remember, West Ham were linked with Stoke City’s winger  Sorba Thomas in the summer – an ex Hammer who has in fact gone to Premier League Hull City and struggled enormously – so much so that footballleagueworld.co.uk claim ‘West Ham dodged huge £10.5 million transfer bullet’:

West Ham made a pretty shrewd decision by backing away from Sorba Thomas and investing in Edvin Austø

We may think things are bad right now, but with youngster Austbo West Ham look to have found a young talent with a high ceiling – compared with the -relatively speaking – wizened old pro’ Thomas who at 27 seems to have peaked, if Hull City’s experience is anything to go by. Good choice, Nils Koppen.

Very easy to hate on all things West Ham just now with the club sitting outside even the play off places. Austbø however continues to shine even on dark days at Ewood Park and needs to be nailed-on as a starter in place of Solomon who, by comparison, just looked plain ordinary.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

The fans are the ones who are a credit to our club Weve proved our loyalty time and time again Waiting to see it from management owners and players

Credit for signing a player who has done what exactly in the second division so far? £20M on Engles, £5m on Solomon and £10m for Piroe had we gone up? I see nothing here to give him credit for. I was chatting to a guy Saturday who told me he thinks West Ham are the easiest team to play through in the league. He reckoned our midfield had zero defensive qualities and constantly left our back four exposed. The more I think about it, the more I see what he is saying. If we had no intention of playing Alvarez or Magassa, why didn’t we sign a midfielder who can defend or tackle because none of the current bunch can.

Promotion has to be the key aim this season, but it was always going to be a reset after the torrid few seasons and incompetent leadership at the club under Sullivan and his managers. I was ok with Nuno staying on, but hindsight always being clear 20/20 vision, I think it was Paco Jémez that was the factor in West Ham’s improvement towards the back end of last season. I hope Parker brings the feelgood factor back to the squad, last seen during the high times of Moyse. Stating the bleeding obvious, there’s still time to push for that automatic spot, but no room now for what we’ve been witnessing recently if it’s going to happen for us.

#2107. Scott Parker Has a Selection Dilemma and the Numbers Are Damning

Plenty has already been written about Mads Hermansen, with transfer speculation continuing to swirl. Reports suggest Newcastle’s Nick Pope could be a target when the January window opens, but for now, West Ham’s goalkeeping situation remains firmly under the spotlight.

The numbers are difficult to ignore. A goalkeeper who isn’t making enough saves and is shipping goals at an alarming rate, 23 conceded in 15 games, is becoming a problem that cannot be overlooked.

One possible solution could be Alphonse Areola, who previously worked under Scott Parker at Fulham. There is also a potential opportunity for highly-rated youngster Finlay Herrick, who may be worth a closer look.

While Areola’s statistics last season hardly inspire confidence, conceding 37 goals in 20 appearances without recording a clean sheet, there is at least some context. By comparison, Hermansen managed seven clean sheets while conceding 28 goals in 18 matches.

The pair offer very different strengths and weaknesses! Areola is arguably the better shot-stopper but struggles when asked to play out from the back. Hermansen, meanwhile, has been preferred for his distribution and comfort in possession, yet questions remain over his save percentage and ability to keep the ball out of the net when it matters most.

Ex-Goalie Nuno failed to get the best out of Hermansen

Another concern is the absence of an established senior goalkeeping coach. That said, it’s worth remembering that the club’s former manager was a goalkeeper himself, while Rui Barbosa brought years of coaching and playing experience. Neither appeared able to significantly influence Hermansen’s development.

Currently, Billy Lepine, a former Dagenham & Redbridge youth player who has worked within the academy setup since 2008, occupies the role. Lukasz Fabianski is also assisting on a part-time basis with the academy.

And perhaps that’s where the story takes an even stranger twist.

Cast your mind back to 4th December 2024, when West Ham travelled to the King Power Stadium. Leicester won 3-1, ending a six-game winless run. On that night, West Ham peppered the Leicester goal with 31 shots, the highest number they had ever recorded in a Premier League match. Ten were on target and they dominated possession with 61%.

Standing between the posts for Leicester that evening?

None other than Mads Hermansen, who produced a performance worthy of Middle-earth, adopting Gandalf’s famous stance of “You shall not pass!” as he admirably defended his goal.

The previous year in the Championship he featured in the EFL team of the season. One of the most proactive ball playing keepers in the league, and completed 13 clean sheets.

If ever there was evidence of the “West Ham goalkeeper curse”, that might just be it.

The solution feels fairly straightforward. Bring Fabianski into the senior goalkeeping coaching setup, get Areola focused solely on football rather than the DJ decks, and bring in an experienced goalkeeper on loan in January to provide competition.

The ball is now firmly in Scott Parker’s court.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

Middle of the park a bigger issue than front and back of the team

A top goalkeeper and a striker should be our priority in January

Now I am not saying Hermansen shouldn’t be relieved of his duties — he should be replaced.

However, last season’s Stats shout out what problems our Goalkeepers face ….. Areloa played his matches with Dinos and Dumbo, whoops sorry, Kilman in front if him, whilst tge majority of Hermansen’s matches had Dinos and Disasi.

Replace Kilman and whichever goalkeeper is in between the Hammers sticjs, will have improved Stats

Does Fabianski still have his boots and gloves? Seriously Herrick is much better at playing out from the back than the other two, he just seems lacking in height for me. Would he dominate his area in a way we have been calling out for this season?

Our “goalkeeper curse” is nothing compared to our “striker curse”.

#2106. Newcastle United Women’s team turn on the style at St James’ Park in another step to the title

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Newcastle United Women’s team faced their Burnley counterparts at St James’ Park on Sunday in this important second tier league match.

With Soffia Kelly’s two week emergency loan spell having ended with the Newcastle United Women’s team, she returned to parent club Aston Villa this week.

In her place came Anna Pederson from Charlton on a one week deal which suggests first choice goalie Anna Tamminen is close to a return.

Beth Lumsden and Martha Thomas have been nominated for October’s WSL 2 Player of the Month award. They face opposition from Ipswich’s Princess Ademiluyi, Elise Hughes of Sunderland, Leticia McKenna of Nottingham Forest and Watford’s Phoebie Poole.

The club have appointed Sarah Lowden as Academy Manager. She arrives from the FA where she spent the past seven years working in a variety of roles developing young players. Although Sarah is from the area she previously worked with academies at Reading and Burton Albion.

“I’m excited to play a key role in the development of the next generation of talented footballers, helping them fulfil their potential both on and off the pitch, while contributing to the continued growth and success of the women’s game at this incredible club.” She said on joining.

Before kick-off there was a minute’s silence for Remembrance Sunday. Female military officers laid a poppy wreath at the centre circle and were led out by Sophie Akrill, who along with serving her country plays football locally for Cullercoats and ice hockey for Whitley Bay Beacons.

Newcastle manager Tanya Oxtoby made just one change from last week, Hungarian central defender Hanna Németh coming in to start her first WSL 2 game, as they lined up in their usual 4-3-3 formation. Burnley went with five at the back and a midfield diamond in front of them, with just a loan striker up top.

All the fans were housed in the East Stand with both the Gallowgate and Leazes closed for this game with newly promoted Burnley.

Sensing there were goals to be had, Newcastle went for the jugular from the off. They nearly took the lead very early on but Jordan Nobbs fired well over from 12 yards after meeting a cutback from the left. Then a cross from the left by Nobbs was deflected over to striker Kathleen McGovern, who couldn’t quite bundle the ball home from point-blank range.

But a minute later the Scottish striker made amends and fired the Lasses into a lead they wouldn’t relinquish. Some neat build up play saw the ball laid back to Lois Joel on the edge of the area, who curled a pass to the back post for McGovern to fire home. The former Hibernian forward seems to love playing against Burnley after she netted a hat-trick against them in a pre-season game at Gateshead earlier in the campaign.

Newcastle were relentless in their pursuit for goals and quickly doubled their lead soon after. Beth Lumsden again worked well down the right channel before creating some space close to the byline. As she tried to cut the ball back for a team mate, former Lasses defender Deanna Cooper appeared to slice at the ball and redirected it past goalie Kirstie Levell.

Ironically it was Cooper’s third goal for Newcastle at St James’ Park, after netting a last minute equaliser against Southampton two seasons ago, and then also finding the net against Sunderland.

The Lady Mags could have added to their lead and perhaps should have been four or five goals to the good before the break. Kaitlyn Torpey found Martha Thomas, whose first-time lay-off to Jordan Nobbs opened up space for a curled effort towards the bottom corner, but she was denied by a stunning save by Levell. Before Thomas headed well wide with another chance three minutes later.

Then as half-time approached, a loose ball in the box fell to midfielder Katie Bradley, who found space between the Burnley defenders but could only stab it around the outside of the foot of the post after Levell had punched McGovern’s cross clear. Newcastle looked certain to add a third on the stroke of half-time but Alethea Paul produced an excellent block to deny Nobbs.

Burnley failed to test Newcastle, and goalie Kayla Rendell could have literally put her feet up and read the newspaper throughout the game, she had so little to do.

However, in Alethea Paul and Emma Siddall they had two very willing runners at wing back and veteran former Manchester United striker Rachel Williams battling away with a physical presence up front.

They threatened for the first time in the 37th minute when Paul’s inswinging corner was met by Williams, but the forward could only direct her header over the bar.

Perhaps Burnley’s best chance came when Siddall advanced well down the right flank leaving the Newcastle defence flat footed. But despite getting in behind the home side’s back four, she was unable to get her strike on target. Her effort sailing over the crossbar.

Charlie Chadwick made a difference when she came on to play on the left of midfield, firing wide from 20 yards soon after arriving.

But Newcastle made it three with half an hour to go when Lumsden charged towards goal once again before finding league top scorer Martha Thomas who controlled well before finding the net at the Gallowgate end from six yards out.

A flurry of substitutions saw some of the rhythm go out the game with a whole new front three up top for the lasses. However, Freya Gregory did star in her 25 minute cameo as she had a couple of efforts that narrowly cleared the bar.

Tyler Toland deflected a couple of Newcastle shots, before Levell produced another fine stop to keep out a fierce angled drive from Gregory. Then Jessie Gale, also on and playing up top, squandered an opportunity to make it four, failing to connect with Gregory’s cross.

Burnley then suffered a further setback when Charley Docherty, who had been on the pitch for just 20 minutes, limped off with an apparent hamstring injury. The Clarets, who only had five outfield players named on their bench, had to play on with ten players after they had already used up all their allocated substitutions.

Nobbs, who started Newcastle off on the right track, had the final say when she forced a comfortable save from Levell in the closing stages. While Cooper produced a crucial block to deny McLaughlan from close range as Newcastle saw out the victory.

Newcastle United: Kayla Rendell, Rachel McLauchlan (c), Hanna Németh, Gemma Evans, Kaitlyn Torpey, Katie Bradley (Mollie Lambert 63), Lois Joel, Jordan, Nobbs, Beth Lumsden (Oona Sevenius 69), Martha Thomas (Jessie Gale 69), Kathleen McGovern (Beth Lumsden Freya Gregory 63).

Subs not used: Anna Pedersen, Charlotte Wardlaw, Jemma Purfield, Hildur Antonsdóttir, Aoife Mannion.

Burnley: Kirstie Levell, Emma Siddall, Jessica Hennessy, Deanna Cooper, Naomi Hartley (Charley Docherty 65), Alethea Paul, Brenna McPartlan, Tyler Toland, Jamie Finn (Charlie Chadwick 55), Christie Harrison-Murray, Rachel Williams (Brooke Cairns 80).

Subs not used: Jackie Burns, Kiera Sena, Maddi Wilde.

Where that leaves Newcastle United Women’s team

Newcastle remain unbeaten in WSL2 and have a three point cushion over second placed Sunderland after the Lady Black Cats won the River Wear derby in Durham. Elsewhere, Ipswich finally lost their unbeaten start to the season after they slipped up to an in-form Bristol City.

There are 15 league games remaining with only top spot good enough for automatic promotion to the top flight this season.

Teams that finish second and third will play off for the right to face the team that finishes second bottom of WSL1 and a chance at promotion, although that represents a much tougher route.

Newcastle travel to the Stadium of Light for next Sunday’s top of the table clash with Sunderland. The Lasses have already faced their local rivals once this season and lost 1-0 at Gateshead in the League Cup so they will be looking to put things right this time in the league encounter.

United are next at home the following Sunday when they host Nottingham Forest in a League Cup group game at Gateshead International Stadium.

#2105. Report claims winter move could rescue West Ham player from year-long ordeal in east London

There’s increasing consternation that some of the signings from last season are proving inadequate even for this, the second division of English football. This site’s opinions over Pablo Julio are well known and well documented – the bearded one is a trier but still plays as if he’s a member of the crowd who’s won a lucky programme raffle to play with the big boys each time he appears in a West Ham shirt.

Perhaps even more concerning is Taty Castellanos’ failure to make any impact whatsoever on this West Ham side following relegation. The Argentine attacker has just one goal to his name this season – from memory his yellow cards now out score his goals – and he merely struts around looking angry each time he’s called upon without contributing significantly to the team output. How the recruitment team will be wishing they’d cashed-in on the reported £40 million Everton interest on deadline day.

Options may be on the horizon for a January exit – it appears Taty still has his admirers: Sportwitness.co.uk make the claim:

“River Plate have identified West Ham United‘s Valentín Castellanos as the ‘top target’ for the winter market as part of their plan to strengthen their attack.

His contract lasts until 2030, with an option for another year, and Transfermarkt value him at €28m. The frontman’s contract and salary he earns with Scott Parker’s side are the ‘main obstacles’ for River Plate.

Therefore, the Argentine club are considering alternatives like signing him on loan with a fee or buying a percentage of his rights. This is only possible if the London club were to give their approval.”

Whether there’s any real mileage in the River Plate interest, it may well be that West Ham at least have a bargaining chip to try and negotiate a sale of Castellanos in January which would more than likely suit player and club. Taty can then find a league in which his talents are more suited and West Ham can source a front man which will better  suit Scott Parker’s playing style.

#2104. Rangers hero makes ‘ruthless killer’ forward plea as Celtic pressure builds

Former Rangers striker Kris Boyd would like the club’s current forwards to develop a “ruthless” streak as he claimed they were in the ascendancy in the title race.

Ryan Naderi took his tally for the season to nine goals in Rangers’ 2-0 win over St Mirren on Saturday while Kevin Kelsy has struck five times in 10 appearances.

But with attacking midfielder Kim Min-su still to get off the mark and winger Badredine Bouanani on one goal, Boyd feels Rangers can step up another level.

“Rangers could quite easily have won by four or five on Saturday night,” said Boyd, who struck 300 career goals.

“I don’t quite know what it is because you look at Bouanani and Kim Min-su and you feel as if there are players in there who are contributing.

“But I think in the modern game you’re looking and saying, can their numbers increase? Of course they can.

“When you look at Naderi at the weekend, he takes his penalty superbly well, but he could quite easily have walked off with the match ball.

“Kevin Kelsy is a threat and he’s shown that over the period of time he’s been here.

Kevin Kelsy celebrates with Ryan Naderi (Image: Stuart Wallace / Shutterstock)

“Rangers are creating chances, but I don’t see that ruthless killer at the top end of the pitch that is obsessed with scoring goals and that’s all they want to do. Maybe it’s just me, I’m not sure there are many of them in the modern game right now.

“But I would like to see somebody step forward and be that man who wants to go and score every single week, wants to get a second, get a third and get a fourth, because there are chances being created.

“I don’t think you can knock what the two strikers have done because when Derek (McInnes) left Kelsy out at Dundee, Rangers didn’t look the same team. I thought they struggled at Dundee for large parts.

“So you can’t criticise because I think both of their contributions have been very good. With (Youseff) Chermiti and (Lawrence) Shankland out, it’s important they continue that.”

Rangers are four points adrift of William Hill Premiership leaders Celtic but they have a game in hand.

Boyd said: “The start that Rangers had wasn’t great, but they’ve managed to correct that and they’re definitely a team that’s in form and don’t look as if they’re going to lose games of football.

“Rangers have had a lot of tough away games and you’d expect them to keep this run going. Rangers do seem as if they’re the team in the ascendancy and they’ve got that belief behind them.

“Whereas with Celtic, they’re winning games of football, maybe not convincingly, but you feel as if there’s just a crisis around the corner. It seems to be that with any dip, it’s a full-blown attack on the board, a full-blown attack on the manager and then the players get it.”

Kris Boyd was speaking at the announcement of William Hill as official sponsor of Walking Football Scotland. To find your nearest game visit walkingfootballscotland.org

There’s a certain perspective on this weekend’s defeat now, the dust having settled on the Ewood Park 2-1 loss and the furious away fans now returned back to their day jobs. In the cold light of day this would seem to be a drama, not a crisis – West Ham are ninth in the division, sure, but still just six points off second spot.

Yes there’s a drama at east London, as most neutral’s favourites for automatic promotion continue to stumble. But six points can easily be recovered over the hectic schedule in the run up to Christmas. Maybe a reminder to us all to take a breath, check the table again at the end of the year – and let Scott Parker do his thing in the meantime.

#2101. Glaring summer 2026 Newcastle United transfer window blind spot now costing NUFC dear

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

The summer 2026 Newcastle United transfer window was incredibly busy.

A time of massive change at St James’ Park.

So many new Newcastle United signings coming in, even more players leaving.

The squad had a very different look once the Newcastle United transfer window closed in early September.

Fans left to evaluate the newcomers that we would be relying on to help navigate the 2026-27 season.

This is a breakdown of that Newcastle United transfer window when it comes to the signings made, the transfer fees are based on what was generally reported and they include the reported potential future add-ons in each case.

Goalkeepers £24.6m Ewen Jaouen, £25.7m Lukas Hornicek

Midfielders £23m Sean Steur, £35.5m Aladji Bamba, £52m Nico Gonzalez, £3m Ousmane Diabaté

Attacking players £43m Bazoumana Toure, £51m Matias Fernandez-Pardo

For me, there is a glaring summer 2026 Newcastle United transfer window blind spot that is now costing NUFC dear.

It feels like a lifetime ago now but let me take you back to the start of the 2025-26 Premier League season.

In the opening five Premier League matches of last season, Newcastle United kept four clean sheets.

In the opening 16 matches in all competitions of the 2025-26 season, Newcastle United kept seven clean sheets, The 16th game of last season was a 2-0 Champions League home win over Athletic Club.

As for the final 42 games of Newcastle United’s 2025-26 season, how many clean sheets were there?

The 4 January 2026 we had Newcastle 2 Crystal Palace 0, 18 January 2026 it was Wolves 0 Newcastle 0, 21 January 2026 we watched Newcastle 3 PSV 0, then 14 March 2026 we had Chelsea 0 Newcastle 1.

Only four clean sheets in the final 42 matches of Newcastle United’s 2025-26 season!

So for me, there is a glaring summer 2026 Newcastle United transfer window blind spot.

In such a busy summer window, there were nine signings made but only one defender.

Amar Dedic signed at full-back, but you also have to note that in that summer window, United got the likes of Kieran Trippier, Emil Krafth and Matt Targett off the books. Whilst Alex Murphy went out on loan for this season.

This 2026-27 season so far, Newcastle United have conceded 21 goals in 13 matches and still haven’t kept a clean sheet at home since January, ten months ago! If you don’t keep a clean sheet then you have to score at least two goals to stand any chance of winning.

Newcastle United don’t do grinding out 1-0 victories!

The last 1-0 United win at St James’ Park was against Wolves, Nick Woltemade’s scoring debut on 13 September 2025! Just the 14 months ago.

Away from home this season, Newcastle United have actually kept three clean sheets and all these matches ended unsurprisingly in victories. We have had 2-0 away wins at both Palace and Spurs in the league, plus a 1-0 at Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

On the Monday (10 March 2025) before the Carabao Cup final win over Liverpool, Newcastle won 1-0 away from home at West Ham in the Premier League thanks to a Bruno goal. That was exactly 20 months ago today, since then Newcastle have only had the three 1-0 victories, home or away (Wolves home in September 2025, away at Chelsea in March 2026, then Millwall away in September 2026).

We all know that the UEFA SCR impact meant Newcastle United had to sell some high transfer fee players and get a fair few high wage players off the books, whilst recruiting younger generally lower transfer fee and wage players to rebuild the squad.

However, it is baffling why more of the available resources wasn’t aimed at improving the defence. Especially when it is seen as far easier to find far better value in the overseas markets when recruiting promising defenders, than is is to land promising young players to score and create goals.

I am always generally wary of this modern trend of having a Sporting Director dictating which signings are targeted, rather than the manager being the main man.

For me the jury is very much out on Ross Wilson and the decisions he made this summer, both players sold and bought in.

The manager is surely far better placed to know the priorities in terms of positions that need strengthened and the players who can best fill them.

Wilson’s decision making means that when it comes to the back four, Newcastle United are still relying on the same four central defenders that were here last season when only four clean sheets in the final 42 games of the 2025-26 campaign.

Lewis Hall is the only left-back, whilst at right-back we now have Amar Dedic and the rarely fit enough to play Tino Livramento.

The ‘planning’ appears to be that if Dedic and Tino can also play left-back if needing to, whilst Lewis Miley can act as an emergency right-back. This can all swiftly fall apart though as we have already seen. With Tino unable to get and stay fully fit this season as he was injured in the summer, it means that Dedic gets injured and already we have Miley having to be right-back, which also then prevented him getting a run in the team where he needs to be in midfield AND where the team need him! Whilst we have been lucky that Lewis Hall is the team’s best player and hasn’t got injured, yet.

Meanwhile in the centre of defence, only 13 matches gone so far and a case of shuffling deckchairs around on the Titanic with no combination so far really convincing from the same quartet who were here last season! They include Schar and Burn who both turn 35 this season and surely at least one young promising central defender should have arrived in the summer window, both for this season AND the future.

#2095. Time to make the best use of West Ham’s talisman – before we wear him out

Strikers, you would think, tend to have longer careers than wingers. West Ham’s own top scorer in the Premier League was himself a converted full back-stroke-winger who became the ‘beast’ that was Michael Antonio. And the chances are, he’d have seen his career curtailed long before the car crash that almost cost him his life, if he’d been hurtling up and down the wing all afternoon, twice a week for half a dozen years.

As it was, his hamstrings needed their own private treatment regime but West Ham managed to keep him in one piece long enough for him to notch sixty eight Premier League goals – still just a club record.

But it got me thinking, Jarrod Bowen hits thirty this year. You can see where I’m going with this.

West Ham are too reliant upon Jarrod Bowen and need to plan to help him work smarter, not just harder.

The player who David Moyes signed in 2020 has won us a trophy, run his legs off and contributed blood, sweat, toil and tears for this club and still he’s there every match day, tackling back, doing his defensive duties, then haring up the other end and assisting or bearing down on goal himself. Oh and we made him skipper too just for good measure. An awful lot on our star man’s shoulders.

Is that the best use of Bowen as he leaves his ‘twenties behind? West Ham have no understudy, no support act ready to step into that right wing position to give him a breather or a chance to move centrally and become the ‘converted’ striker his first West Ham manager David Moyes used to churn out – be it Antonio, Arnautovic or, back at Everton now, Thierno Barry, his latest ‘convert’  to the striker role.

Perhaps Bowen needs a more central role? Perhaps West Ham need another winger to offer Scott Parker the chance to move Bowen inside, as he does with Manor Solomon on the left.

After all, our leading scorer and ‘assists’ king can’t influence games if he’s mired in tracking back down at the wrong end of the pitch. And he’s not getting any younger.

You can play episode 15 on the audio player above or use your favourite podcast platforms including Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, YouTube, and Acast.

Listen to the latest episode of The Mag Pod! Join Jamie, Simon, and Hutch for unfiltered football debate.

Newcastle United’s frustrating draw at Fulham, a worrying lack of goals and an increasingly uncomfortable Premier League position dominate Episode 15 of The Mag Pod.

Jamie Smith is joined by Simon Cahill and David Hutchinson to assess the Magpies’ latest performance before delivering their quarter-season report cards, picking Newcastle’s standout players and signings, and debating whether this campaign could yet end in European qualification or a relegation battle.

The 1-1 draw at Craven Cottage provides plenty to discuss. Jacob Murphy’s spectacular strike earns praise, but Fulham’s equaliser, Harvey Barnes’ missed opportunities and Dan Burn’s controversially disallowed goal leave the lads wondering whether Newcastle have thrown away another valuable two points.

There’s particular concern about Newcastle’s attacking options. With goals proving difficult to come by, the panel questions whether the current forwards can provide what the team needs, while Hutch delivers a particularly unforgiving assessment of Harvey Barnes. Murphy’s celebration also comes under the microscope, prompting a wider discussion about supporters’ expectations and the criticism facing established members of the squad.

With ten Premier League matches played, it’s time for the first proper assessment of Newcastle United’s season. Jamie, Simon and Hutch reveal their grades, nominate their highlights, choose their best summer signings and identify their players of the season so far. Lewis Hall, Sean Steur and Lukas Horníček all feature in the conversation.

Looking ahead, the mood ranges from cautious optimism to outright pessimism. Could Newcastle recover sufficiently to challenge for European football, or is a relegation battle becoming a genuine possibility? And with Sunderland looming on the fixture list, there’s plenty of anxiety about what the coming months might bring.

There’s the usual humour, disagreements and increasingly desperate attempts to find positives, as the lads consider what supporters can realistically hope for from the rest of the season.

#2093. Confession shows former favourite’s love affair with West Ham continues from afar

It has taken three years for West Ham to spiral from the summit of their footballing prowess to the depths of second division mediocrity, and the Hammers’ experiences can serve as a cautionary tale to any other poorly run Premier League side. Complacency and poor decision making will destroy even the best – supported side in the blink of  an eye.

Hammers fans have also taken years to process the sale of their most successful captain since Billy Bonds, the Chairman announcing his availability the very day after their Europa Conference League trophy sale. For that alone, I’ll never forgive Sullivan.

There are ways of doing things. and that isn’t it.

As supporters we are now getting used to seeing Declan Rice in an Arsenal kit, and for many – most, I’d guess, but not all.. there’s a vicarious sense of pride still for the former Hammer, although of course not his club, as he goes onto deserved success.

It is clear the players’ love for West Ham hasn’t diminished either. Speaking to GQ magazine, Declan professed:

““I obviously love West Ham so much still, still a massive part of my life, I still watch them.”

Picking out his favourite goal ever, Rice glossed over those Champions League free kicks and confessed a goal in Claret and Blue meant more to him:

“My favourite goal is when I was playing for West Ham in the Conference League,” Rice said. “I picked the ball up on the edge of our own box and ran the whole pitch. As I was running forward I just remember the stadium getting louder and louder and louder, and as I scored the goal the place just erupted.

So I think that was one of my best solo goals.”

Leopards, it is said, do not change their spots. Neither, it would seem, do out-of-favour ‘wantaways’ who refuse to play for one manager having fallen out with his predecessors, despite being made a millionaire by the club that employs him, change their mindsets.

Such would seem to be the case with the talented yet angst-ridden package that is Jean Clair Todibo, once of Barcelona, now of West Ham yet loaned out through sheer frustration to Lens back in his native France.

…Lens boss Yannick Cahuzac has played down West Ham United loanee Jean-Clair Todibo being angry about being substituted off against Lille and insists the defender’s fitness is being worked on.

On Friday, against Lille, the West Ham centre-back started the game and he was substituted in the 62nd minute mark, a decision which left the player visibly frustrated and angry. “

Todibo now on loan at French side Lens but still not pulling up any trees: Is anyone surprised?

Revealing that even now, two and a half years since Todibo’s arrival at West Ham, the player is still not fit for a full game. Surprise, surprise.

Did he ever manage 90 minutes in a West Ham shirt? I think maybe just once. Some players have ‘trouble’ all over them and Todibo, ever since his Barcelona exit, has struggled to find a place where he can hold down a squad place and keep his seemingly volatile nature in check.

#2090. Success story means West Ham flop could stay away for ever – Report

If ever there was a story detailing the importance of attitude over ability, then this tale of overcoming adversity – in the end –  involving one of West Ham’s worst transfers of the Steidten era – is certainly that.

Having vowed never to write another Niclas Fullkrug story I find myself drawn yet again to his remarkable mental resilience and fortitude, re-launching his career at 34 years old ‘back home’ in Germany after failing so conclusively at both West Ham and AC Milan – just in case anyone wants to point the finger at a Hammers’ coaching failure being solely to blame for his misfiring.

This is a player who lost his international squad spot, couldn’t stay fit for love nor money (although he had plenty of that) and eventually after a very public, failed loan in Italy, rediscovered himself and his form back in his Bundesliga home.

Life in the old dog yet at 34 – Niclas Fullkrug

Fullkrug is now the German top league’s top scorer. Just reflect on that for a second.

The guy who scored three times in two years as a West Ham player. Probably he’d have done better without missing half the club’s games through injury. As Bild.de suggest, Fullkrug has found his happy place and may never leave:

“It is possible!:Will Füllkrug stay with Werder forever?”

Runs their headline, confirming that they want to keep ‘Fulle’ even once his playing days are over:

“There have already been talks about a follow-up contract with us and the idea is still concrete. It is quite conceivable that we will tie him to the club after his career. I really appreciate his football expertise.”

Which suggests that Fullkrug has already done enough to earn another deal at Werder Bremen, meaning he’s likely never, ever coming back. Sadly, neither is the £27 million, or the nine million salary which he’s had as a West Ham player – thats three million per goal. Nice work if you can get it.

#2088. Mika Baur Celtic injury latest as midfielder pulls out of Germany under-21s squad

Mika Baur has been ruled out of Germany's under-21s squad for coming fixtures following his injury suffered against Kilmarnock.

The midfielder has had a strong campaign for the Hoops so far and become one of the standouts in the engine room with his performances.

He went down at Parkhead with what looked like a sore one after being caught by Aaron Tshibola of Killie in the second-half of his side's 1-0 victory in Glasgow.

Manager Martin O'Neill confirmed Baur, 22, would undergo scans on his ankle to determine the extent of the issue. And having been called into the Germany under-21s set-up by head coach Antonio Di Salvo, the football federation confirmed this afternoon that he had to withdraw.

Ahead of clashes with Belgium and Croatia, a short injury updated provided read: "Lukas Ullrich, Mika Baur, and Arijon Ibrahimovic are unfortunately unavailable. We have called up Tom Rothe, Kofi Amoako, and Maurice Krattenmacher as replacements.

"Furthermore, we currently don't know if Karim Coulibaly will be available, as he is showing symptoms of illness. We will have to wait until tomorrow to see if he is available."

It remains to be seen how long, if at all, Baur will be sidelined at Celtic but leaving the international camp provides him with the opportunity to potentially rehab the possible strain quickly.

One way or another, Scott Parker is going to be forced to make changes to his starting eleven against Preston North End when the International break concludes in a little under two weeks’ time.

One player will be sitting out the tie with an enforced suspension after picking up his fifth yellow card this season. It actually gives Parker a big opportunity to try out an alternative pairing at the heart of his defence, without knocking the confidence of his gentle giant Maximilian Kilman who will miss the game.

Airidas Golambeckis has already impressed: perhaps Kilman’s suspension is his moment..

Whether Parker picks Brazilian centre back by trade Morato or teen Hammer Airidas Golambeckis, the Irons’ manager cannot go wrong. If his pairing produces a shut-out then he’d be justified in retaining his inspired ‘pick’ and leaving Kilman on the bench.

If whoever partners Mavropanos doesn’t cover themselves in glory then he can return to Kilman for the following fixture against Portsmouth just three days later.

Either way, it gives fans like me a respite from the endless starting of a tried, tested, and found wanting duo appearing yet again on the team sheet.

There is , too, the hope that an alternative for Kilman might be lurking within the squad, ready and waiting for just such an opportunity. It seems that Ezra Mayers found his way into Parker’s thinking through being in the ‘right place at the right time’: Perhaps Morato or Golambeckis can make the jersey their own? We can but hope.

#2084. Newcastle star Amar Dedic sparks six-car police swoop after being spotted with a BOW AND ARROWS in Northumberland beauty spot before weapon is seized

Published: 13:29 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 17:28 EST, 5 November 2026

Newcastle United star Amar Dedic was at the centre of a major police operation after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows at a Northumberland beauty spot – with at least SIX patrol cars involved in the search for the £30million defender.

The Bosnia international sparked alarm when a concerned member of the public reported seeing him and a friend walking with the weapon near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the area in Harlow Hill, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were finally intercepted around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Sources have described the dramatic swoop on Dedic's vehicle before officers searched the car and seized a bow and arrows, with the 24-year-old questioned about his activities.

In a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic. It is understood the pair were in the area by chance and stopped to offer assistance.

After speaking to the two men, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public, with police subsequently stating that the equipment was believed to have been intended for recreational use.

Amar Dedic played in Newcastle's 1-0 defeat by Everton on Monday evening

Dedic was spotted with a crossbow off Military Road, the 61-mile B6318 in Northumberland

However, enquiries remain ongoing into the incident, which happened on Wednesday afternoon. It is understood that Dedic and his friend had fired some arrows while in the countryside, although it remains unclear what they were aiming at. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in the UK.

Dedic joined Newcastle from Benfica during the summer and has impressed at right back despite the club's difficult start to the season.

Daily Mail Sport understands he will not face disciplinary action from Newcastle over the incident, although there is a feeling that the player was naive to believe he could walk around the countryside carrying such weaponry.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: 'Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

'Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing.'

Dedic is expected to be available for Saturday's Premier League trip to Fulham, where Newcastle will attempt to halt a run of four defeats in five matches across all competitions.

#2083. ‘They deserve it’ – Kostas Tsimikas admits familiar failing cost Liverpool in Istanbul

Kostas Tsimikas admitted that Liverpool got what they deserved in their 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce in Istanbul on Wednesday.

The Reds were in front twice at the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium but still contrived to come away with nothing against Dirk Kuyt’s side, who claimed all three points thanks to Vedat Muriqi’s 79th-minute header.

Jeremy Jacquet was criticised for turning his back on Mason Greenwood’s free kick for the first equaliser, and Alisson Becker was culpable of poor positioning for Archie Brown’s goal to make it 2-2.

Speaking to UEFA.com after the match, Tsimikas magnanimously conceded that Fenerbahce were full value for their win and lamented Liverpool’s defending over the goals that they shipped.

The Greek defender said (via BBC Sport): “Congratulations to Fenerbahce, they deserve it. We didn’t play how we had to play. We didn’t defend after the goal we conceded. After three or four minutes, automatically we conceded another goal.

“I think we have to mark better if we want to win games. We didn’t play very good and that’s why we lost.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

It sums up how careless Liverpool were this evening that they were in the lead twice and occupied a winning position for only eight minutes against Fenerbahce, with the goals from Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak cancelled out all too quickly.

The manner of all three goals that the home side scored will enrage Iraola – it wasn’t as though the Istanbul outfit had to produce moments of magic to inspire their way to victory over the Reds.

Tsimikas himself was far from convincing, enduring a ‘tough night’ in the words of Liverpool Echo reporter Paul Gorst as he struggled to contain the threat of Greenwood, and he ended up being substituted for Milos Kerkez with 15 minutes remaining.

Liverpool have now conceded 10 goals in their four Champions League matches, shipping three for the third European fixture in a row, a record which’ll surely concern the head coach at this phase of the competition.

The debrief from this game will not be a pleasant one, and a much better defensive performance will be required if the Reds are to return to winning ways against Crystal Palace on Sunday.
